Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following landforms is spread over the largest area in the oceans?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Ocean Basin. The distribution of oceanic 
landforms is as follows – 
• The world's widest continental shelf is the Siberian 
Shelf (1500 km, Arctic Ocean). 
• Between 20°N and 60°S latitudes, oceanic plains are 
most widely spread. 
• Between 60°N and 70°N latitudes, oceanic plains are 
absent.

Hydrosphere.q: Consider the following statements regarding the development of coral reefs and select the correct answer using the codes given below: 1. Corals mainly form in tropical oceans and seas.2. Corals are not found in deep seas; they are found at depths of 60-77 meters below sea level. 3. Oceanic salinity between 27‰ to 30‰ is suitable for coral growth. 4. Rising sea temperatures are very beneficial for coral algae, causing them to turn white. ` Code:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
1, 2, and 3 are correct. Corals are mainly 
found in tropical oceans, as they require high 
temperatures (20°C to 21°C) to survive. However, they 
do not thrive in extreme heat or cold. Corals are found 
at shallow depths of 200-250 feet (60-77 meters). 
Excessive oceanic salinity is harmful to corals, and the 
optimal salinity for coral growth is 27‰ to 30‰. A rise 
in sea temperature initiates coral bleaching, turning 
corals white, disrupting photosynthesis, and eventually 
leading to coral death.

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following statements about corals is/are correct? (1) Corals are mainly found in tropical oceans and seas, where the average annual temperature is between 20°C and 21°C. (2) Oceanic salinity between 30‰ and 34‰ is ideal for coral growth. Select the correct answer from the codes given below:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Due to global warming, the Indian Ocean is 
the most affected by coral bleaching (El Niño also 
contributes to this). 
The optimal salinity for the growth of coral reefs is 
27%0 to 30%0.

Hydrosphere.q: Arrange the following seas in the correct west to-east order:
options: Caspian Sea, Mediterranean Sea, Black Sea, Aral Sea
Black Sea, Mediterranean Sea, Caspian Sea, Aral Sea
Black Sea, Mediterranean Sea, Aral Sea, Caspian Sea
Mediterranean Sea, Black Sea, Caspian Sea, Aral Sea
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The correct west-to-east order of the seas is: 
Mediterranean Sea → Black Sea → Caspian Sea → 
Aral Sea

Hydrosphere.q: Cape Verde is an island group located in –
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Atlantic Ocean 
Cape Verde is an archipelago in the Atlantic Ocean, 
located about 570 km off the western coast of Africa, 
near Senegal, Gambia, and Mauritania. The largest 
island in the Cape Verde archipelago, based on size and 
population, is Santiago, which is home to the nation's 
capital, Praia.

Hydrosphere.q: Extensive terrestrial deposits are found near:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Extensive terrestrial deposits are found near 
Eastern archipelagos. On land, the process of 
weathering causes rocks to break down and fragment 
into fine to coarse pieces, which are called terrestrial 
deposits. In the sea, the deposition of these materials is 
categorized, meaning larger particles settle near the shore 
while finer materials move farther into the sea. Based on 
particle size and chemical composition, terrestrial deposits 
are classified as gravel, sand, and silt.

Hydrosphere.q: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the codes given below: List-I (Oceanic Deposits) List II (Origin) A Littoral deposits 1 Shells of planktonic mollusks B Abyssal deposits 2 Extremely fine clay rich plant residues C Pteropod Ooze 3 Remains of marine organisms and plants D Diatom Ooze 4 Algal types Codes A B C D
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The correct matching is: 
• Littoral deposits → Remains of marine organisms 
and plants 
• Abyssal deposits → Algal types 
• Pteropod Ooze → Shells of planktonic mollusks 
• Diatom Ooze→Extremely fine clay-rich plant residues 
Note: Organic materials in marine deposits originate 
from the sea itself. Neritic deposits include skeletal 
remains of organisms and plant material, while pelagic 
deposits mainly consist of algal remains.

Hydrosphere.q: The submerged part of a continent is called:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The submerged part of a continent is called 
the continental shelf. Its average depth is 100 fathoms 
(600 feet or 200 meters), with an average slope between 
17 feet or 1° to 3°. The width of the shelf is influenced 
by terrestrial coastal relief. The continental shelf 
occupies about 8.6% of the total ocean floor, extending 
over 13.3% of the Atlantic, 5.7% of the Pacific, and 
4.2% of the Indian Ocean.

Hydrosphere.q: Who is considered the father of modern oceanography?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
John Murray is regarded as the father of 
modern oceanography. Through the Challenger 
expedition (1841–1914), he discovered the Wyville 
Thomson Ridge in northern Scotland. He studied 
plankton, marine sedimentation, coral reef formation, 
and their origin. He proposed the Plankton Theory and 
created depth maps of deep-sea regions.

Hydrosphere.q: Abyssal plains are found in:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Abyssal plains are found in deep-sea plains. 
These are the most extensive regions of the ocean floor, 
with depths ranging between 3,000 to 6,000 meters. 
They cover about 75.9% of the total ocean floor, with 
their extent being 80.3% in the Pacific, 80.1% in the 
Indian Ocean, and 54.9% in the Atlantic Ocean.

Hydrosphere.q: What is known as the "rainforest of the sea"?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Coral reefs are called the "rainforests of the 
sea" because they exhibit greater biodiversity than 
tropical evergreen forests. Coral reefs contain around 
1,000,000 species, of which only 100,000 species have 
been studied. Coral reefs are found between 25°N and 
25°S latitudes at depths of 200 to 250 feet (60–77 
meters). Ideal conditions for coral reef formation 
include temperatures of 20°–21°C and salinity 
between 27 to 30 ppt.

Hydrosphere.q: The "Dolphin Rise," part of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, is located:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Dolphin Rise, part of the Mid-Atlantic 
Ridge, is located north of the equator. The Mid
Atlantic Ridge is the most prominent feature of the 
Atlantic Ocean, extending 14,400 km from Iceland in 
the north to Bouvet Island in the south. The portion 
north of the equator is called Dolphin Rise, while the 
southern part is known as the Challenger Rise.

Hydrosphere.q: The Great Barrier Reef is located:
options: Off the western coast of Europe
Off the eastern coast of North America
Off the eastern coast of Asia
Off the eastern coast of Australia
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Great Barrier Reef is found off the 
eastern coast of Australia. A barrier reef is a large 
and extensive coral reef that runs parallel to the coast 
but remains separated by a lagoon. It is the largest 
coral reef system in the world.

Hydrosphere.q: Who proposed the "Subsidence Theory" regarding the formation of coral reefs?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Charles Darwin proposed the Subsidence 
Theory of coral reef formation in 1837, later refined it 
in 1842. His observations were based on studies of 
Bikini Atoll in the Marshall Islands. According to this 
theory, the formation of coral reefs is linked to land 
subsidence. Coral polyps grow in warm, shallow 
marine areas mainly on the eastern coasts of 
continents due to ideal temperature and salinity 
conditions maintained by trade winds. 
Other theories on coral reef formation:

Hydrosphere.q: What is the particle size in "ooze" deposits?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The particle size in "ooze" deposits is less 
than 0.005 mm. Pelagic deposits found in deep-sea 
areas contain fine-grained materials called ooze, which 
settle as marine sediments. These are classified into two 
types:

Hydrosphere.q: The extensive area between the continental shelf and the abyssal plain is known as:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The steeply sloping zone between the 
submerged shore and the deep oceanic plains is called 
the continental slope. Notably, sediment deposition is 
absent on the slopes due to their steep incline, 
preventing debris from settling. The average slope is 
between 2° and 5°, with depths ranging from 200 
meters to 3000 meters. Continental slopes cover 
approximately 8.5% of the total oceanic area, with the 
greatest extension found in the Atlantic Ocean (12.4%). 
Note: The edge of the slope marks the termination of 
continents, where canyons and trenches are also found.

Hydrosphere.q: Considering the distribution of freshwater on Earth, which of the following is correct? 1. Groundwater - 29.9% 2. Glaciers - 68.7% 3. Lakes - 2.5%
Hydrosphere.explanation:
About 97.5% of the total volume of water on 
Earth is found in the oceans, remaining 2.5% is fresh 
water. Glaciers contain 68.7% of fresh water and 
groundwater contains about 29.9% of fresh water. 
Lakes and rivers contains about 1.4% of fresh water.

Hydrosphere.q: According to Murray's classification of oceanic sediments, the blue-black color of blue mud is due to:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
All materials accumulated on the ocean floor 
are termed oceanic sediments. Murray and Renard 
provided specialized information on this subject. Based 
on particle size, texture, and chemical composition. 
Oceanic materials are categorized into gravel, sand, and 
mud. Mud particles are finer than clay. Based on color, 
they are classified as blue, green, and red mud. Blue 
mud is formed in calm waters through chemical 
weathering and contains iron sulfide and iron oxide, red 
mud contains iron oxide, and green mud contains 
potassium silicate and iron.

Hydrosphere.q: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge, north of the equator in the Atlantic Ocean, is known as:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Mid-Atlantic Ridge extends in an 'S' 
shape from Iceland in the north to Bouvet Island in the 
south, covering a length of 14,400 km, and never 
descends below 4000 meters from the seafloor. 
Although it tilts westward or eastward at times, it 
always retains its central position. North of the equator, 
this ridge is known as the Dolphin Rise, while south of 
the equator, it is called the Challenger Rise. Between 
Iceland and Scotland, it is termed the Wyville Thomson 
Ridge. South of Greenland, the ridge widens into what 
is called the Telegraphic Plateau.

Hydrosphere.q: What is the shape of the Atlantic Ocean?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The shape of Atlantic Ocean is of an ‘S’ 
shaped. 
It extends between Europe and Africa to the east and 
Americas to the west.

Hydrosphere.q: The part of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge located north of the equator is called:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
North of the equator Mid-Atlantic ridge is 
known as the Dolphin Rise, while south of the equator, 
it is called the Challenger Rise. Between Iceland and 
Scotland, it is termed the Wyville Thomson Ridge. 
South of Greenland, the ridge widens into what is called 
the Telegraphic Plateau.

Hydrosphere.q: The formation of the continental shelf is primarily due to which of the following processes?
options: Deposition of black soil near the sea
Normal faulting along the continental margin
Erosion of the coastline due to rising sea level
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Normal faulting along the continental margin 
plays a crucial role in the formation of continental shelf 
because of the process of crustal extension and 
subsidence. Normal faulting initiates the structural 
foundation while sedimentation shapes the flat 
submerged shelf.

Hydrosphere.q: The Pacific Ocean is connected to the Arctic Ocean through:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Bering Strait connects the Pacific Ocean 
to the Arctic Ocean and separates Alaska in North 
America from Russia in Asia. It runs parallel to the 
International Date Line. 
A strait is a narrow waterway connecting two large 
water bodies, usually situated between two landmasses. 
It is crucial for international maritime transportation.

Hydrosphere.q: The Glacial Control Theory was proposed by:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Glacial Control Theory was proposed by 
R.A. Daly in 1915 when he observed that coral reefs in 
the oceans formed after the Pleistocene Ice Age. During 
this Ice Age, seawater turned into ice, causing a decline 
in sea level by about 33 to 38 fathoms. This exposed 
coastal shelves and platforms, which were later 
submerged again when ice melted, leading to the 
formation of coral reefs.

Hydrosphere.q: Which scholar proposed the Glacial Control Theory of coral reef formation?
Hydrosphere.explanation: See explanation in the previous question.

Hydrosphere.q: A reef separated from the mainland or inland shore by a deep lagoon is called:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Coral reefs are formed by the accumulation 
and consolidation of coral polyps’ skeletons. These 
corals thrive in warm tropical waters and rely on 
calcium carbonate. 
A coral reef located parallel to a coastline but separated 
by a lagoon is called a barrier reef. It is the longest, 
broadest, and highest of all coral reefs. 
The world’s largest barrier reef is the Great Barrier 
Reef off the eastern coast of Australia, stretching 1,920 
km from 9° to 22°S latitude.

Hydrosphere.q: The Great Barrier Reef is located in:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The world’s largest barrier reef is the Great 
Barrier Reef off the eastern coast of Australia, 
stretching 1,920 km from 9° to 22°S latitude.

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following trenches are located in the Pacific Ocean? A. Kuril B. Puerto Rico C. Kermadec D. Tonga
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Oceanic trenches are the deepest parts of the 
oceans, covering about 7% of the ocean floor. They are 
mostly found along coastal mountain belts. There are 32 
trenches identified in the Pacific Ocean, with the 
western part having the highest number. Some of the 
major ones include: 
• Mariana Trench - 11,022 meters 
• Tonga Trench - 10,882 meters 
• Kuril Trench - 10,498 meters 
• Kermadec Trench - 10,047 meters 
• Aleutian Trench - 7,679 meters

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following is NOT a basin of the eastern Atlantic Ocean?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Labrador Basin 
The eastern Atlantic Ocean contains basins such as the 
Canary Basin, Spanish Basin, Cape Verde Basin, 
Angola Basin, and Guyana Basin. The Labrador Basin 
is located in the western Atlantic Ocean.

Hydrosphere.q: What does the hypsographic curve represent? A. Continental shelf B. Continental slope C. Deep sea plain D. Salinity changes in sea water.
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The hypsographic curve represents the 
elevation of land and the depth of oceans. It includes 
features such as the continental shelf, continental slope, 
and deep ocean plains.

Hydrosphere.q: Albatross plateau is located in-
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Albatross plateau, also known as East pacific 
Ridge, is located in pacific ocean which is spread over a 
width of 1600 km. Between 23° to 35° south latitudes, it 
has two branches, the eastern branch of which goes 
towards the Chilean coast and the western branch goes 
south wards in the name of Eastern Island Ridge. New 
Zealand Ridge, Queensland plateau and Hawaiian 
Ridge are the prominent other ridges of the pacific 
ocean.

Hydrosphere.q: How much area of the ocean floor does the continental slope cover?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The continental slope is spread over 8.5% of 
the ocean floor, the slope between the submerged coast 
and the deep ocean plain is called the continental slope. 
Its slope varies at different places. Its average slope is 
2° to 5° and depth is between 200m to 3000 m.

Hydrosphere.q: Cocos ridge is located in:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Cocos ridge in the Eastern Pacific Ocean 
expands from isthmus of central America to Galapagos 
island. 
Note:- Other ridges of pacific ocean- 
(i) Albatross Ridge. 
(ii) Newzealand Ridge 
(iii) Queensland Ridge 
(iv) Hawaiian Ridge

Hydrosphere.q: The Largest continental shelf is-
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The part of margins of the continents which is 
submerged in ocean water, the average depth of water 
on it is 100 fathoms (1 fathom = 6 feet) and slope is 
between 1° to 3° is called continental shelf. The width 
of the shelf is controlled by coastal topography. The 
mountainous areas along the coast, the shelf is narrow 
and on contrary it is more extensive. Generally the 
width of the shelf is 80 km. Ex the widest Siberian shelf 
is up to 1500 km.

Hydrosphere.q: The widest continental shelves are associated which part of the world:
Hydrosphere.explanation: See the explanation of the above question.

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following oceanic trenches is the deepest?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Mariana Trench 
The Mariana Trench is the deepest oceanic trench on 
Earth, with a depth reaching approximately 11,022 
meters at the Challenger Deep.

Hydrosphere.q: Deepest point of Atlantic Ocean-
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Oceanic trenches is the deepest part of the 
ocean which is spread over 7% part of oceanic plain. It 
is situated along the coast in front of mountain ranges. 
Their slopes are steep, Deep trenches are also seen 
along the islands. Due to the absence of new folds along 
the coast of the Atlantic Ocean, trenches are found less. 
According to murray, 19 trenches are found at a depth 
of more than 3000 fathoms. The major trenches among 
there are Nares trench Puerto Rico trench, Romanche 
trench, Waldivia, Buchanan, Moseley etc. 
Note:- The deepest point in the Atlantic Ocean is the 
Puerto Rico trench (8385 m).

Hydrosphere.q: Select the correct code- List-I List-II A Lord Howe Ridge i. South Atlantic Ocean B. Wyville Thomson Ridge ii. South west Pacific Ocean C. Walvis Ridge iii. North Atlantic Ocean D. Prince Edward Crozet Ridge iv. South-west Indian OceanCode: A B C D
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The correctly matched sequence is as 
follows- 
Oceanic Ridge Location 
Lord How Ridge South west pacific Ocean 
Wyville Ridge North Atlantic Ocean 
Walvis Ridge South Atlantic Ocean 
Prince Edward South west Indian Ocean 
Crozet Ridge

Hydrosphere.q: The Aleutian and Mariana trenches were formed by
options: Along the transform fault plate margin
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Aleutian and Mariana trenches are 
formed along the convergent plate margins. Convergent 
plate margin are also called destructive plate margins. 
In this, when two plates move towards and collide with 
each other, the heavier plate is sub-ducted beneath the 
lighter plate. Oceanic trenches and volcanic islands are 
formed by the convergence of two oceanic plates.

Hydrosphere.q: Examine the following statements and select the correct answer using the code given below. (A) Atolls are ring-shaped islands of coral reefs. (B) Submerged volcanic island with flat tops are guyots (C) The average slope of the slopes in the ocean is about 10 degree. Code:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
(A) and (B) 
The average slope of continental slope is 2° to 5° 
• Submerged island or mountains formed by volcanoes 
with flat tops are known as guyots. 
• Horse shoe or ring shaped coral reefs are called 
atolls. Atolls are ring shaped island of coral reefs.

Hydrosphere.q: Match of following: List-I (Oceanic Ridge) List-II (Ocean) A Dolphin i. Southern Indian Ocean B. Scotia ii. Southern pacific Ocean C. Saint Paul iii. Southern Atlantic Ocean D. Albatross iv. Northern Atlantic Ocean Code: A B C D
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The correctly matched sequence is as follows- 
Oceanic Ridge Ocean 
Dolphin Northern Atlantic Ocean 
Scotia Southern Atlantic Ocean 
Saint Paul Southern Indian Ocean 
Albatross Southern Pacific Ocean

Hydrosphere.q: Consider the following statement and select the correct answer from the code given below. Statement (A): Atolls are circular in shape Reason (R): The formation of coral reefs found tectonic theory. Code:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The shape of an atoll is circular. In the pacific 
ocean, the important Atolls are Bikini Atoll near 
Hawaian island, Fiji Atoll, Cook Atoll near Caroline 
island, Ellice island near Funafati Atoll.

Hydrosphere.q: Saint Paul ridge is located-
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Saint Paul ridge is located in Indian Ocean. 
• Other ridge of Indian Ocean- 
Chagos Island, 90° East Ridge, Prince Edward Crozet 
ridge etc.

Hydrosphere.q: The Strait of Gibraltar, having a strategic location, connects-
options: Sea of Japan and Yellow sea
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Gibraltar Strait separates Spain from morocco 
and connects Mediterranean sea to North Atlantic Ocean. 
This strait is known as 'key of Mediterranean'. Korean 
strait connects Japan sea and Yellow sea and separates 
Tsushima Island and South Korea.

Hydrosphere.q: The depth of Photic zone is between-
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The depth of the photic zone is found up to 
200 meters, vegetation and corals etc, are found up to 
this depth. This zone is called the neartic zone.

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following ooze has the highest deposits in the Atlantic Ocean?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Globigerina ooze has the highest deposits in 
the Atlantic ocean. 
• Globigerina oozes are formed by the cells of micro
organisms of a species called Foraminifera. 
• Radiolarian ooze is a silica rich ooze. 
They are mainly found at a depth of 2000-5000 fathoms. 
Hydrosphere 328

Hydrosphere.q: The substances of pelagic deposits are obtained from:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Pelagic deposits include the remains of algae 
found in the deep sea, which are present in the form of 
ooze. They are classified into two types based on the 
amount of lime and silica: 
(i) Lime-rich ooze 
(ii) Silica-rich ooze

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following are siliceous oozes? A. Pteropod B. Diatom C. Globigerina D. Radiolarian
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Ocean floor sediments are known as oceanic 
deposits. Due to the high silica content, they are called 
'siliceous ooze.' Because of the lack of lime, this ooze 
does not dissolve quickly and is found at great depths in 
both warm and cold seas. Siliceous ooze is of two types:

Hydrosphere.q: The most widespread oceanic sediment deposit is:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Oceanic deposits are formed by the 
accumulation of sediments on the ocean floor. The most 
widespread oceanic deposit is Globigerina. 
Globigerina ooze is mainly formed from the shells of 
Globigerina organisms. It is a lime-rich pelagic deposit 
found in deep ocean basins. It covers 25 million square 
miles in the Pacific Ocean, 14.7 million square miles in 
the Atlantic Ocean, and 12.2 million square miles in the 
Indian Ocean. 
Pelagic deposits are classified into:

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following landforms is associated with the ocean floor?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Trench is associated with the ocean floor. The 
Mariana Trench (Challenger Deep) is the deepest trench 
in the world, located in the Pacific Ocean, with a depth 
of 11,022 meters. Skerry, stack, and meander are 
landforms created by erosional forces.

Hydrosphere.q: The deposits formed from algae (or moss) in benthic deposits are mostly in the form of liquid mud, called:
Southern Pacific Ocean Code: A B C D
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The correct matching pairs are: 
• Sunda Trench - Eastern Indian Ocean 
• Mariana Trench - Northern Pacific Ocean 
• Puerto Rico Trench - Northern Atlantic Ocean 
• Atacama Trench - Southern Pacific Ocean

Hydrosphere.q: Which type of oceanic deposits covers the largest area on the ocean floor?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Organic deposits cover the largest area on the 
ocean floor. 
• Organic deposits are classified as follows: 
Organic Deposits 
(i) Lime Rich (ii) Silica Rich 
a. Globigerina ooze a. Diatom ooze 
b. Pteropod ooze b. Radiolarian ooze

Hydrosphere.q: What are the flat-topped underwater mountains called?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Flat-topped underwater mountains are called 
guyots. 
• Guyots (submarine plateaus) are important for coral 
development as they provide a base for coral reef 
formation. 
Hydrosphere 329

Hydrosphere.q: What is the depth of the continental shelf?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The continental shelf is the submerged part of 
the continental margin with a slope of 1° to 3° and an 
average depth of 200 meters or 600 feet. 
Note: 1 fathom = 6 feet

Hydrosphere.q: Southern Atlantic Ocean D. Nares Trench 4. Northern Atlantic Ocean Codes: A B C D
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The correct matching pairs are: 
• Tonga Trench - Southern Pacific Ocean 
• Challenger Trench - Northern Pacific Ocean 
• Romanche Trench - Southern Atlantic Ocean 
• Nares Trench - Northern Atlantic Ocean

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following deposits are found in the deepest parts of the oceans?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Red Clay is found in the deepest parts of the 
oceans. 
• Red Clay contains a high amount of iron oxide and 
aluminum, which gives it a red color. 
• This soil originates from the decomposition of 
volcanic material, which is carried into the oceans by 
rivers or wind. 
• The formation of this clay includes deposits from 
volcanic eruptions, as well as iron, silicate, and 
aluminum (85.35%), calcium (6.7%), and remains of 
silica-containing organisms (2.39%).

Hydrosphere.q: The widest continental shelves are found in:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
A continental shelf is the submerged edge of 
a continent with a slope of 1 to 3 degrees and a depth of 
about 200 meters (100 fathoms). The widest shelf in the 
world is the Siberian Shelf. 
• The widest continental shelf is found in the Arctic 
Ocean, along the Siberian coast and extending into the 
North Polar Sea.

Hydrosphere.q: Coral reefs are made up of:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Coral reefs are made up of coral polyps. 
• Coral reefs are marine landforms formed by the 
accumulation of the skeletal remains of coral 
organisms, composed of limestone and dolomite. 
• Coral polyps live inside calcium carbonate shells, and 
their bodies host numerous algae called zooxanthellae.

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following statements is NOT true?
options: The continental shelf is a submerged extension of the continent.
The continental shelf is made of granite.
The continental slope is part of the continent.
The widest continental shelf is in the Atlantic Ocean.
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The widest continental shelf is not in the 
Atlantic Ocean but in the Arctic Ocean.

Hydrosphere.q: Globigerina deposits are classified as:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Globigerina ooze is a calcareous deposit 
containing 64.47% calcium carbonate and 1.64% silica. 
• Globigerina organisms are typically found at depths 
of 2000 to 4000 fathoms. 
• These deposits are abundant in the tropical and 
temperate zones of the Atlantic Ocean, the eastern 
and western continental shelves of the Indian Ocean, 
and the eastern Pacific Ocean.

Hydrosphere.q: Atolls are found in the highest numbers in:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Atolls are most commonly found in the 
Pacific Ocean. 
Major atolls include Bikini Atoll near the Hawaiian 
Islands, Fiji Atoll, Cook Atoll near Caroline Island, and 
Funafuti Atoll near Ellice Island.

Hydrosphere.q: Examine the following statements and choose the correct answer based on the given codes: A. Fringing coral reefs are attached to land. B. Barrier reefs are separated from land by a lagoon. C. The Great Barrier Reef is located east of New South Wales. D. An atoll is a ring-shaped island.
options: A, B, and C are correct.
A, B, and D are correct.
B, C, and D are correct.
A, B, C, and D are correct.
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Fringing coral reefs form along the steep 
continental shelves and remain submerged underwater, 
creating a narrow and shallow lagoon known as a "boat 
channel." 
• Such reefs are found near Florida, the Andaman and 
Nicobar Islands, Malaysia, and the Sakau Islands. 
• The world's largest barrier reef, the Great Barrier 
Reef, is located east coast of the Queensland, 
Australia—not New South Wales. 
Hydrosphere 330

Hydrosphere.q: Among the major oceanic relief features, which covers the largest area?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Abyssal plains cover the largest area among 
oceanic relief features. However, their proportion varies 
among different oceans: 
• Continental Shelf – 8.6% 
• Continental Slope – 8.5% 
• Abyssal Plain – 75.9% 
• Ocean Trench – 7%

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following is the most extensive oceanic relief feature?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Abyssal Plains (refer to the explanation 
above).

Hydrosphere.q: Neritic (coastal plankton) deposits are primarily related to:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Neritic deposits primarily originate from the 
dissolution of marine organisms' skeletons.

Hydrosphere.q: Two statements are given below, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Choose the correct answer from the codes given below: Assertion (A): Coral reefs are predominantly found in the eastern parts of the oceans in tropical regions. Reason (R): The optimum temperature for coral growth ranges between 18°C to 30°C. Codes:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) correctly explains (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) does not correctly explain (A).
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Coral reefs in tropical regions are found 
mainly between 25° latitude on either side of the 
equator, where geographical conditions necessary for 
their growth are available. Corals are predominantly 
found in the eastern parts of continents, not oceans, due 
to the presence of warm ocean currents, which create 
favorable conditions for their development. 
Coral reefs thrive in warm water, with optimal 
temperature between 18°C to 30°C. 
Hence, Assertion is incorrect and Reason is correct.

Hydrosphere.q: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below: List-I (Rivers) List-II (Water body at the mouth) A. Orinoco 1. Gulf of Guinea B. Niger 2. Pacific Ocean C. Volga 3. Atlantic Ocean D. Amur 4. Caspian Sea Codes: A B C D
Hydrosphere.explanation:
• The Orinoco River originates in the Eastern 
Andes of Colombia and flows into the Caribbean Sea 
(Atlantic Ocean). 
• The Niger River originates from the Loma Mountains 
on the Sierra Leone-Guinea border and empties into the 
Gulf of Guinea. 
• The Volga River originates from the Belarus Plateau 
in Russia and empties into the Caspian Sea. 
• The Amur River flows into the Pacific Ocean.

Hydrosphere.q: A chain of small atolls with shallow lagoons is called:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
A chain of small atolls with shallow lagoons 
is called ‘Faros.’ 
• An atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef surrounding a 
lagoon, often forming around a submerged plateau. 
• When atolls are aligned in a series, they are known as 
Faros coastal coral reefs.

Hydrosphere.q: What is the primary cause of coral bleaching?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The primary cause of coral bleaching is 
global warming. 
• Coral bleaching refers to the whitening of corals due 
to the loss of symbiotic algae, which results in the death 
of coral polyps. 
•The first recorded observation of coral bleaching was 
made by Alfred Mayer in 1919.

Hydrosphere.q: A submerged sea mount with a flat top is called:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
A submerged seamount with a flat top is 
called a Guyot. 
• Guyots resemble underwater mountain peaks and 
provide a habitat for coral growth. 
Hydrosphere 331

Hydrosphere.q: Clive Wilkinson was associated with:
options: Global Coral Reef Monitoring Network (Townsville, Australia)
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Clive Wilkinson was associated with the 
Global Coral Reef Monitoring Network (Townsville, 
Australia).

Hydrosphere.q: What is the average depth of the Atlantic Ocean?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The average depth of the Atlantic Ocean is 
3900 m. 
•The Atlantic Ocean covers 1/6th of the Earth's surface 
and is half the size of the Pacific Ocean.

Hydrosphere.q: Which type of sediment has the largest spatial distribution in the Pacific Ocean?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Red clay has the largest spatial distribution in 
the Pacific Ocean. 
• It consists of aluminum silicates and iron oxides, 
found at depths greater than 2700 fathoms.

Hydrosphere.q: One of the major mid-ocean ridges is found in:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
One of the major mid-ocean ridges is found 
in the Central Atlantic Ocean.

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following seas is the shallowest?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Yellow Sea is the shallowest. 
• Yellow Sea: 152 m 
• Baltic Sea: 459 m 
• North Sea: 661 m 
• Black Sea: 1100 m

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following seas is the least deep?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Yellow Sea is the shallowest. 
• Yellow Sea: 152 m 
• Baltic Sea: 459 m 
• North Sea: 661 m 
• Black Sea: 1100 m

Hydrosphere.q: What is the correct sequence from land to sea?
options: Continental slope → Abyssal plain → Ocean depth → Continental shelf
Continental shelf → Continental slope → Abyssal plain → Ocean depth
Ocean depth → Abyssal plain → Continental slope → Continental shelf
Abyssal plain → Ocean depth → Continental slope → Continental shelf
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The correct sequence is: 
Continental shelf → Continental slope → Abyssal plain 
→ Ocean depth.

Hydrosphere.q: Which marine feature is NOT conducive to rapid coral reef development?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Coral reefs develop in marine environments 
where water conditions are suitable for calcium 
carbonate deposition. They require sunlight and do not 
thrive in highly polluted or excessively clear waters. 
While they grow near island shores, small channels, and 
lakes, their development is not possible on guyots and 
seamounts.

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following lakes has the largest surface area?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Lake Baikal has the largest surface area. 
• Baikal: 31,500 km² (approx) 
• Chad: 25,760 km² (approx) 
• Titicaca: 8,135 km² (approx) 
• Nicaragua: 8,135 km² (approx)

Hydrosphere.q: Match List I with List II and choose the correct answer from the codes given below: List-I (Mid-Ocean Ridge) List-II (Ocean) A. Carlsberg Ridge i. Pacific Ocean B. Mid-Atlantic Ridge ii. Antarctic Ocean C. East Pacific Ridge iii. Indian Ocean D. Antarctic Ridge iv. Atlantic Ocean Codes: A B C D
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The correct matches are: 
• Carlsberg Ridge – Indian Ocean 
• Mid-Atlantic Ridge – Atlantic Ocean 
• East Pacific Ridge – Pacific Ocean 
• Antarctic Ridge – Antarctic Ocean 
Additionally: 
• 90° East Ridge – Indian Ocean 
• Challenger Ridge – South Atlantic Ocean 
• Dolphin Ridge – North Atlantic Ocean

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following coasts has a narrow continental shelf?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
A narrow continental shelf is observed on the 
western coast of South America, where countries like 
Peru and Chile are located. The most extensive 
continental shelf is found in the Arctic Ocean.

Hydrosphere.q: What is responsible for global changes in sea level?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Eustatic (global) sea level refers to changes in 
the ocean's volume due to variations in the total amount 
of water in the oceans. It is not a physical level but a 
representation of sea level if all ocean water were 
contained in a single basin. Eustatic sea level follows 
the "bathtub approach" and is affected by factors such 
as glaciation and ocean water temperature.

Hydrosphere.q: Match List-I with List-II: List-I (Seafloor Features) List-II (Ocean) A. Socotra-Chagos Ridge i. Arctic Ocean B. Svalbard Ridge ii. Indian Ocean C. Mid-Atlantic Ridge iii. Atlantic Ocean D. Cocos Ridge iv. Pacific Ocean Codes: A B C D
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Correct Answer: 
Socotra-Chagos Ridge - Indian Ocean 
Svalbard Ridge - Arctic Ocean 
Mid-Atlantic Ridge - Atlantic Ocean 
Cocos Ridge - Pacific Ocean

Hydrosphere.q: Ekman transport occurs in which of the following?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The concept of Ekman transport was 
introduced in 1902. It states that wind is the primary 
source of energy for ocean circulation. Ocean currents 
are influenced by wind friction, which affects water 
layers up to 10-100 meters deep.

Hydrosphere.q: What type of graph represents the relative proportion of surface areas at different elevations?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The average depth of oceans is 3,800 meters, 
while the average land elevation is 840 meters. The 
elevation and depth of land and ocean are represented 
by a hypsometric curve.

Hydrosphere.q: What is the method to represent different elevations or depths of land above a reference level?
Hydrosphere.explanation: Refer to the explanation above.

Hydrosphere.q: What does the hypsometric curve represent?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The hypsometric curve represents both land 
and underwater elevation in a combined manner.

Hydrosphere.q: Where is the Kermadec Trench located?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Kermadec Trench is located in the 
southwestern Pacific Ocean. Other notable trenches in the 
Pacific include the Aleutian Trench, Kuril Trench, 
Philippine Trench, Mariana Trench, and Atacama Trench.

Hydrosphere.q: Which island is known for its saltwater resources?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Isle of Man, located in the UK, is known 
for its saltwater resources.

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following islands is NOT located in the Atlantic Ocean?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Baffin Island, Hispaniola, and Cuba are 
located in the Atlantic Ocean, whereas Java is situated 
in the Indian Ocean.

Hydrosphere.q: Match List-I with List-II: List-I (Oceanic Trenches) List-II (Depth in meters) A. Tonga i. 7,760 B. Kuril-Kamchatka ii. 10,540 C. Philippine iii. 10,880 D. Romanche iv. 10,500 A B C D
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The depth of trenches are follows- 
Oceanic Trenches Depth (meter) 
Tonga 10,880 
Kuril-Kamchatka 10,500 
Philippine 10,540 
Romanche 7760

Hydrosphere.q: What is the correct sequence of coastal zones from land to the deep sea?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The sequence from land to sea follows: 
Backshore → Foreshore → Nearshore → Offshore.

Hydrosphere.q: What are the causes of wave formation in the ocean?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Ocean waves are generated due to seasonal 
effects, cyclonic effects, and volcanic activity.

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following pairs is incorrectly matched?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Tonga Trench is located in the Southern 
Pacific Ocean, not the Atlantic.

Hydrosphere.q: What is the correct sequence of sediment deposition from the coast to the deep sea? 1. Clay 2. Mud 3. Sand 4. Silt
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The correct order is: 
Sand → Silt → Clay → Mud

Hydrosphere.q: Which statements about submarine canyons are correct? (1) They are long, narrow, and deep valleys. (2) They are mostly found in deep-sea plains. (3) They are more commonly found along rugged coastlines. (4) According to W.M. Davis, they are formed due to turbidity currents.
Hydrosphere.explanation:
1 & 4 
Submarine canyons are narrow, deep and steep-walled 
valleys on the continental shelf and slope, they are also 
called canyons. According to Davis, Ridder and Daily, 
Submarine caves are formed due presence of excessive 
water and strong waves near the remnant coast.

Hydrosphere.q: The formation of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge is a characteristic example of: 1. Convergence 2. Divergence 3. Erosion 4. Seafloor spreading Code:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Mid-Atlantic ridge is an example of divergent 
plate boundaries and seafloor spreading. 
The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is a continuous underwater 
mountain range that stretches through the Atlantic 
Ocean, formed by tectonic plates moving apart at 
divergent boundary.

Hydrosphere.q: The continental shelf is determined by which depth contour line?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The average depth of the continental shelf is 
200 meters (600 feet). 
 (1 fathom = 6 feet)

Hydrosphere.q: Northern Atlantic Ocean Codes: A B C D
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The correctly matched pairs are: 
Oceanic Ridges Ocean 
Dolphin Ridge Northern Atlantic Ocean 
Challenger Ridge Southern Atlantic Ocean 
Laccadive Chagos Ridge Arabian Sea 
Kerguelen-Gaussberg 
Ridge 
Indian Ocean

Hydrosphere.q: Where is the world's widest continental shelf found?
options: In the Yellow Sea of South Korea
Near the Arctic coast of Norway
Hydrosphere.explanation:
According to given options, world's widest 
continental shelf is found near the Arctic coast of 
Norway.

Hydrosphere.q: Consider the following statements and choose the correct answer using the code given below: 1. The continental slope is an extended part of the continental shelf. 2. Submarine trenches are the most prominent features of the continental slopes. 3. Continental slopes are a result of marine erosion and river deposition. 4. India has extensive continental slopes. Code:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The continental slope is an extended part of 
the continental shelf, and continental slopes are a result 
of marine erosion and river deposition. Hence, the other 
statements are incorrect.

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following is NOT a part of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Kerguelen-Gaussberg Ridge is located in the 
Indian Ocean, whereas Challenger Rise, Dolphin Rise, 
and Wyville Thomson Ridge are parts of the Mid
Atlantic Ridge.

Hydrosphere.q: Ross Ice Shelf is a part of which region?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Ross Ice Shelf is located around the 
Antarctica continent, where glaciers extend towards the 
equatorial regions of the oceans. 
This is part of Southern Polar region.

Hydrosphere.q: The oceanic ridge Dolphin Ridge is located in:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Dolphin Ridge is located in the North 
Atlantic Ocean and the Challenger Ridge in the South 
Atlantic Ocean. 
Major features of the Atlantic Ocean floor include: 
• Telegraphic Ridge (Plateau) 
• Wyville Thomson Ridge 
• North Mid-Atlantic Ridge 
• Dolphin Rise 
• Challenger Ridge

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following oceanic deposits is an abyssal (non-calcareous) deposit?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Red clay is an abyssal (non-calcareous) 
oceanic deposit. Among inorganic substances, red clay 
is the most important because it is found over the largest 
areas of deep-sea deposits. It primarily consists of 
aluminum silicates and iron oxides.

Hydrosphere.q: The Dolphin-Challenger Ridge is located in—
Hydrosphere.explanation:
In the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, the uplifted area 
extending southward from the equator to approximately 
20°S is called the Challenger Ridge. The uplifted area 
between 5°N and 15°N is called the Dolphin Rise.

Hydrosphere.q: The world's largest reserve of the purest freshwater is located in—
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Antarctic continent covers an area of 
approximately 13,209,000 square kilometers, with an 
average ice sheet thickness of about one mile. The 
extensive and scenic iceberg formations in its 
surrounding oceans are notable. Antarctica holds the 
world's largest freshwater reserve because it remains 
largely free from human pollution.

Hydrosphere.q: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge was formed by which geological process?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
From the perspective of plate tectonics, the 
Atlantic Ocean is divided into two parts. Due to the 
westward movement of the American Plate, the 
constructive plate boundaries allow magma to emerge 
from the asthenosphere, leading to the formation of the 
Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

Hydrosphere.q: In the deep ocean, oozes are formed by the deposition of—
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The ocean floor is composed of basaltic rocks. 
Due to the absence of erosion processes within the 
ocean, inorganic rock particles are not found. Therefore, 
the oozes (deep-sea sediments) that accumulate on the 
ocean floor primarily consist of decomposed organic 
matter.

Hydrosphere.q: Where is the deposition of pelagic materials found?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Pelagic materials are known as "deep-sea 
materials." These are organic deposits formed by algae 
(phytoplankton). They are also referred to as "oozes" 
and are found in deep oceans.

Hydrosphere.q: What is the Datum Line?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The datum line is an imaginary line relative to 
which the height and depth of a location are measured. 
It generally represents the mean sea level.

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following is not a deep-sea or pelagic fish?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The pilchard fish is found in shallow coastal 
waters, whereas cod, flounder, and halibut are deep-sea 
or pelagic fishes.

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following is most commonly found in deep-sea deposits?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The most commonly found deep-sea deposit 
is Ooze. These deposits primarily consist of 
microscopic shells of marine organisms. 
Hydrosphere 335

Hydrosphere.q: What is the average depth of Indian Ocean?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The northern shore of Indian Ocean is not 
developed and is fragmented so it is called a semi-ocean. 
The Mozambique channel, Red Sea, Persian Gulf, Arabian 
Sea, Bay of Bengal and Andaman sea are situated on the 
borders of this ocean. Its area is approximately 7.34 crore 
square Km. The average depth is 4000 m.

Hydrosphere.q: What percentage of the Southern Hemisphere is covered by water?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
About 70.8% of Earth's surface is covered 
by water, and 29.2% by land. If we consider only the 
southern hemisphere, then 81% of the total water is 
found in the oceanic regions, making it the dominant 
part of the southern hemisphere.

Hydrosphere.q: During the Challenger expedition, there were between 50° to 60° latitudes: (i) The surface temperature of the water is 12.94°C. (ii) The temperature of water at a depth of 1000 meters was found to be 10.81°C. Choose the correct answer from the following options:-
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Both the statements are incorrect. During the 
challenger expedition, the surface temperature of water 
between 50° and 60° latitudes was found to be 8.94°C 
and a depth of 1000 meter the temperature was found to 
be 4.81°C.

Hydrosphere.q: Which one of the four have maximum constituent of oceanic relief?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Decreasing order. 
Region Percentage 
Abyssal Plain 75.9% 
Continental shelf 8.6% 
Continental slope 8.5% 
Oceanic trenches 7.0%

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following pairs is incorrect? Trench - Ocean
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Challenger Expedition (1884) discovered 
32 trenches in the Pacific Ocean. The Mariana Trench is 
the deepest in the world at 11,022 (or 11,033) meters 
(5,269 fathoms). Other trenches in the Pacific Ocean 
include the Philippine Trench (10,475 m) and the 
Aleutian Trench (7,679 m).

Hydrosphere.q: Which ocean is shrinking every year?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean, 
covering one-third of the Earth's surface, with an area 
larger than all the continents combined. Over the past 
200 years, the Atlantic Ocean has been expanding, 
while the Pacific Ocean has been contracting due to the 
movement of the American Plate.

Hydrosphere.q: The Cayman, Puerto Rico, and South Sandwich Trenches are major trenches of which ocean?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Due to the absence of significant folding 
along the coasts of the Atlantic Ocean, fewer trenches 
are found. According to Murray, there are 19 trenches 
deeper than 3,000 fathoms, including the Puerto Rico 
Trench, Cayman Trench, South Sandwich Trench, 
Nares Trench, and Romanche Trench.

Hydrosphere.q: The second layer of oceanic water is called:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The temperature of ocean water decreases 
with depth. This transition zone, where the temperature 
drops significantly, starts around 100-400 meters below 
the ocean surface and is known as the thermocline.

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following statements is correct? Choose the correct answer using the given codes: 1. The average slope of the continental shelf is between 5° to 8°. 2. The continental shelf is usually wider at river mouths. 3. Submarine canyons are generally found parallel to the continental shelf.
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The continental shelf is an extension of the 
continent covered by ocean water. Its average depth is 
about 200 meters (100 fathoms). The average slope is 
around 1° (17 feet per mile). The continental shelf 
covers 8.6% of the total ocean area, with the Atlantic 
Ocean having 13.3%, the Pacific Ocean 5.7%, and the 
Indian Ocean 4.2%.

Hydrosphere.q: South Pacific Ocean D. Kuril Trench 4. Indian OceanCodes: A B C D
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The correct matching is: 
• Albatross Plateau - South Pacific Ocean 
• Telegraph Plateau - North Atlantic Ocean 
• Amsterdam-Saint Paul Ridge - Indian Ocean 
• Kuril Trench - North Pacific Ocean

Hydrosphere.q: What is referred to as "marine snowfall"?
options: The continuous fall of small marine sediment particles onto the ocean floor.
Continuous snowfall (snowflakes) on the ocean surface.
The sporadic deposition of skeletons from marine nekton organisms onto the ocean floor.
Continuous fall of fine ice particles onto the ocean surface in high latitudes.
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Marine snowfall refers to the continuous 
deposition of microscopic sediment particles onto the 
ocean floor, resembling snowfall on land.

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following is a biogenic marine sediment?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Marine deposits on the ocean floor are known 
as marine sediments. Silica-rich ooze, being less 
soluble, is found in deeper areas. It is classified into two 
types: Radiolarian ooze and Diatom ooze, formed from 
microscopic plant remains.

Hydrosphere.q: The deepest parts of the ocean are found in:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The deepest oceanic regions are found in the 
Pacific Ocean. The Mariana Trench (North Pacific 
Ocean) is the deepest in the world. Other significant 
trenches in the Pacific Ocean include the Aleutian 
Trench, the Philippine Trench, and the Kuril
Kamchatka Trench.

Hydrosphere.q: What is the correct average slope angle of the continental slope?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The correct average slope of the continental 
slope is 4° to 5°. The steep area between the continental 
shelf and deep-sea plains is known as the continental 
slope.

Hydrosphere.q: Regarding the elevation of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge above the Atlantic Ocean floor, which statement is correct?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Mid-Atlantic Ridge extends from Iceland 
in the north to Bouvet Island in the south in an "S" 
shape over a length of 14,450 km. It never dips below 
4,000 meters from the ocean floor, and its height above 
the Atlantic Ocean floor is approximately 3 km.

Hydrosphere.q: Two statements are given below, one is called Assertion (A) and the other is called Reason (R). Choose your answer from the codes given below: Assertion (A): The islands located along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge are highly affected by volcanic activity. Reason (R): Seafloor spreading in the Atlantic Ocean is the main cause of earthquakes.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The islands located along the Mid-Atlantic 
Ridge are highly affected by volcanic activity because 
seafloor spreading in the Atlantic Ocean is the main 
cause of earthquakes. Thus, both the assertion and 
reason are correct, and the reason correctly explains the 
assertion.

Hydrosphere.q: What is the average freezing point of seawater in the Arctic and Antarctic oceans?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The average freezing point of seawater in the 
Arctic and Antarctic oceans is –2°C.

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following is known as a producer in marine ecology?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Phytoplankton is known as a producer in 
marine ecology. It is important to note that all green 
plants are considered producers as they perform 
photosynthesis, converting CO2 and water into glucose 
in the presence of chlorophyll and sunlight.

Hydrosphere.q: In most oceans, where is red clay (Reddish sediment) found?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Red clay is an important inorganic substance. 
In most oceans, it is found in the deepest parts. It is the 
most widespread abyssal sediment.

Hydrosphere.q: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer from the given codes. List-I (Ocean/Sea) List-II (Oceanic Trenches/Depths) A. Atlantic 1. Romanche B. Pacific 2. Challenger C. Indian 3. Diamantina D. Caribbean 4. CaymanCodes: A B C D
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The correct matching is as follows: 
(Ocean/Sea) (Oceanic 
Trenches/Depths) 
A. Atlantic 1. Romanche 
B. Pacific 2. Challenger 
C. Indian 3. Diamantina 
D. Caribbean 4. Cayman

Hydrosphere.q: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer from the given codes. List-I (Ocean/Sea) List-II (Mid-Ocean Ridges) A. Atlantic 1. Aden B. Pacific 2. Cocos C. Arctic 3. Dolphin D. Arabian 4. Mendeleev Code: A B C D
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The correct matching is as follows: 
(Ocean/Sea) (Mid-Ocean Ridges) 
A. Atlantic 1. Dolphin 
B. Pacific 2. Cocos 
C. Arctic 3. Mendeleev 
D. Arabian 4. Aden

Hydrosphere.q: Coral reefs that are typically attached to the shore with an intervening shallow lagoon or channel are called:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Coral reefs that are attached to continental or 
island coasts are called fringing reefs. Although these 
reefs are directly connected to the shore, sometimes a 
small lagoon, called a boat channel, forms between 
them and the land.

Hydrosphere.q: The advance of the sea over land is known as:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The advance of the sea over land is an 
example of positive transgression.

Hydrosphere.q: What is the average depth of the continental shelf?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The depth of the continental shelf, which is a 
gently sloping submerged landmass extending from the 
coast to the continental slope, is approximately 100 
fathoms (600 feet) with a slope of 1° to 3°.

Hydrosphere.q: The deepest ocean trench in the world is:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The deepest ocean trench in the world is the 
Mariana Trench, which is 11,022 meters deep and is 
located east of the Mariana Islands in the western 
Pacific Ocean.

Hydrosphere.q: Where is the Sunda Trench located?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
About 60% of the Indian Ocean's seafloor 
consists of abyssal plains; as a result, there are fewer 
trenches. The Sunda Trench, located near Java Island, 
has a depth of 7,450 meters.

Hydrosphere.q: Where is the Challenger Deep located?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Challenger deep is in the Mariana Trench in 
the Western Pacific Ocean.

Hydrosphere.q: The typical depth range of abyssal plains is:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Abyssal plains are typically 3,000 - 6,000 
meters deep and cover approximately 75.9% of the 
global ocean floor. However, this percentage varies: 
Pacific Ocean - 80.3% 
Indian Ocean - 80.1% 
Atlantic Ocean - 54.9%

Hydrosphere.q: Match List I with List II and choose the correct answer: List-I (Oceanic Trenches) List-II (Location) A. Challenger 1. South Pacific B. Aldrick 2. North Atlantic C. Romanche 3. North Pacific D. Nereus 4. South Atlantic Codes: A B C D
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Challenger - North Pacific 
Aldrick - South Pacific 
Romanche - South Atlantic 
Nereus - North Atlantic

Hydrosphere.q: During which geological period did the ocean attain its present level?
Hydrosphere.explanation: The ocean attained its present level during the Holocene period.The Holocene epoch spans from 10,000 years ago to the present.

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following is the correct order of oceans in increasing size?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The correct order in increasing size is: 
Arctic → Indian → Atlantic → Pacific

Hydrosphere.q: What is represented using isobath lines?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Isobath lines represent the depth of oceanic 
water. 
Lines representing equal salinity levels are called 
Isohaline lines.

Hydrosphere.q: What is the correct order of major oceans by area?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Correct order by area: 
Pacific Ocean → Atlantic Ocean → Indian Ocean → 
Arctic Ocean 
The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest. 
The Mariana Trench is the deepest trench in the world, 
located in the Pacific Ocean.

Hydrosphere.q: What is the map that represents the depths of oceans and seas called?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
A bathymetric map represents the depths of 
oceans and seas. 
A geological map represents the geological formations.

Hydrosphere.q: Where is the Telegraphic Plateau located?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Telegraphic Plateau is in the Northern 
Atlantic Ocean. 
It is also known as the Dolphin Ridge in the North 
Atlantic. 
In the South Atlantic, it is called the Challenger Ridge. 
South of Greenland, this ridge widens and is referred to 
as the Telegraphic Plateau.

Hydrosphere.q: Where is the Aleutian Trench located?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Aleutian Trench is located in the 
Northern Pacific Ocean. 
Other major trenches in the Pacific Ocean include:

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following is incorrectly matched?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Correct matching 
Trench 
Ocean 
Aleutian Trench 
Tonga Trench 
Puerto Rico Trench 
Sunda Trench

Indian Ocean

Hydrosphere.q: The Great Barrier Reef is found off the coast of which Australian state?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Great Barrier Reef is located off the 
coast of Queensland. 
It is the largest coral reef system in the world.

Hydrosphere.q: In which ocean is the Mariana Trench located?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Mariana Trench is in the Western Pacific 
Ocean. 
Other major trenches in the Pacific Ocean include: 
Aleutian Trench 
Kuril Trench 
Japan Trench 
Philippine Trench 
Tonga Trench 
Kermadec Trench 
Atacama Trench

Hydrosphere.q: In which of the following oceans is the 'Sargasso Sea' fully developed?
Hydrosphere.explanation: The 'Sargasso Sea' is fully developed in the North Atlantic Ocean.In the North Atlantic Ocean, there is a gyre formed by the North Equatorial Current, the Gulf Stream, and the Canary Cold Current.Within this gyre, a calm and stagnant area of water exists, where Sargassum seaweed grows abundantly. Due to this characteristic, this part of the ocean is called the Sargasso Sea.

Hydrosphere.q: Choose the correct statement of factors causing variations in salinity: (1) Supply of fresh water by River. (2) Prevailing winds.
Hydrosphere.explanation: For salinity both statements are correct.

Hydrosphere.q: The world biggest ocean water desalination plant is located in:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The would biggest ocean water desalination 
plant is located in Saudi Arabia.

Hydrosphere.q: With regrad to ocean salinity, consider the following statements and choose the correct one. A. Average Chlorinity of the ocean is 19.2‰ B. The belt of highest salinity is found between 20° and 40°N and S latitudes. C. The belt of highest salinity is found between 10° and 20°N and S latitudes. D. Distribution of salinity on the map is shown by means of Isohalines. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
Hydrosphere.explanation:
On maps, the distribution of salinity is shown 
by isohalines (lines of equal salinity). Generally, 
salinity decreases from the equator toward the poles. 
It is important to note that the highest salinity is not 
found at the equator, even though temperature and 
evaporation are high there, because heavy rainfall 
reduces the salinity.

Hydrosphere.q: Identify the correct statements with reference to temperature and salinity of the oceans A. The oceans in the Northern Hemisphere are slightly cooler than those in the Southern Hemisphere. B. The annual range of temperature in the Atlantic Ocean is larger than in the Pacific Ocean. C. The areas of highest salinity in the open oceans are associated with sub-tropical high pressure area. D. The high salinity of Black-Sea is due to influx of large volumes of water by rivers. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The ocean temperatures in the Northern 
Hemisphere are higher than those in the Southern 
Hemisphere. The average annual temperatures of the 
Northern and Southern Hemispheres are approximately 
19.4°C and 16.1°C, respectively. This difference arises 
due to the unequal distribution of land and water in the 
two hemispheres. The annual temperature range in the 
Atlantic Ocean is higher than in the Pacific Ocean. In 
the open oceans, the regions with the highest salinity are 
in subtropical high-pressure areas. Generally, the 
salinity of open oceans ranges from 33‰ to 37‰ 
because evaporation exceeds precipitation. The salinity 
of the Black Sea is lower due to the large influx of 
freshwater from rivers, not higher. Therefore, 
statements (A) and (D) are incorrect, while statements 
(B) and (C) are correct.

Hydrosphere.q: Identify the correct statements with reference to Oreanic Salinity A. Salinity in oceans is maximum in Doldrums B. Salinity in Red Sea is more than in China Sea. C. Salinity is high in the northern part of the Caspian Sea due to high rates of evaporation D. Salinity in Bering Sea is more than in Baltic Sea. Choose the correct from the options given below :
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Salinity in the doldrums is minimal, not 
maximal, because high temperatures and evaporation 
are offset by rainfall, which reduces salinity. The Red 
Sea has higher salinity compared to the China Sea. In 
the northern part of the Waspian Sea, salinity is minimal 
(14‰) due to the supply of freshwater from rivers such 
as the Volga and Ural, whereas in its southern part, in 
the Gulf of Karabugan, salinity is 17‰. Salinity in the 
Bering Sea is higher compared to the Baltic Sea. 
Generally, the total amount of dissolved solids in one 
kilogram of seawater is called seawater salinity, 
expressed in ‰.

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following is NOT correct about density of ocean water?
options: Density gradient is greatest in the Pycnocline layer
Density of ocean waters has no role in vertical and horizontal movements of water.
A T-S diagram facilitates identification of water masses in ocean.
Temperature, salinity and density are used to identify water masses in the ocean.
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Pycnocline Layer is found in ocean 
waters at depths between 300 and 1000 meters, where 
the density gradient of seawater is highest. The T-S 
(Temperature-Salinity) diagram of seawater helps in 
identifying different water masses. Temperature, 
salinity, and density are the main factors used in 
identifying water masses. The vertical and horizontal 
movements of seawater are largely controlled by its 
density, as density determines and regulates ocean 
circulation. 
Hydrosphere 340

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following statement is not correct?
options: Temperature and density are generally inversely related in oceanic water
When salinity increases, density of oceanic water also increases
Pressure and density of oceanic water are directly related
Temperature of oceanic water below freezing point increases its density even more
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Temperature of oceanic water below freezing 
point increases its density even more. 
• Option (d) is incorrect. 
• Temperature is the primary controlling factor of 
density of seawater. 
• The density of warm water is less than that of cold 
water. 
• Pressure is directly and positively related to ocean 
water density through its compressive effects. 
• Salinity is directly positively related to seawater 
density.

Hydrosphere.q: What is the name for the phenomenon characterized by unusually warm ocean temperatures in the equatorial Pacific region
options: More than one of the above
Hydrosphere.explanation:
El Niño is a complex weather phenomenon 
that recurs every 5–10 years. It causes droughts, floods, 
and extreme weather in different parts of the world. In the 
eastern Pacific Ocean, it appears near the coast of Peru as a 
warm ocean current. El Niño is simply an extension of the 
equatorial warm current, which temporarily replaces the 
cold Peruvian or Humboldt current. This current increases 
the water temperature near the Peruvian coast by up to 
10°C. Its effects include:

Hydrosphere.q: The line which joins equal salinity line is known as:
options: More than one of the above
Hydrosphere.explanation:
A line connecting points of equal salinity is 
called an isohaline. A line connecting points of equal 
pressure is called an isobar, and a line connecting points 
of equal temperature is called an isotherm.

Hydrosphere.q: At which of the following latitudes is the smallest change in temperature of oceanic water is observed with increasing depth?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
North Pole 
The smallest change in temperature of oceanic water 
with increasing depth is observed at the North Pole. 
This is because polar regions, particularly the North 
Pole, have consistently cold surface waters due to the 
presence of ice and low solar radiation. As a result, the 
temperature gradient (thermocline) with depth is 
minimal compared to lower latitudes, where surface 
waters are warmer and exhibit a more pronounced 
temperature drop with depth.

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following Sea has the highest salinity?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Dead Sea 
Among the given option Dead Sea has the highest 
salinity. Dead Sea has 238% salinity.

Hydrosphere.q: Salinity is expressed as the amount of salt in gram dissolved in sea water
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Salinity is expressed as the amount of salt in 
gram dissolved in sea water per 1000 grams. Salinity is 
the term used to define the total content of dissolved 
salts in seawater. it is usually measured in g/L or g/kg.

Hydrosphere.q: With reference to the thermocline, consider the following statements : 1. It is transitional zone between the surface waters of the ocean and the deeper layers. 2. The temperature of water changes suddenly with increasing depth. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The thermocline represents the layer in a 
body of water where temperature gradients are steep, 
effectively separating the warmer surface layer from the 
colder and deeper water. 
• This transitional zone is crucial in under-standing 
ocean stratification. 
• Within the thermocline, there is a rapid decrease in 
temperature as depth increases, 
Hence, both statements are correct.

Hydrosphere.q: The water of which of the following water bodies is the saltiest?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The Dead Sea is the saltiest large water body 
on Earth, with salinity around 238%, for higher than 
oceans or other salt lakes.

Hydrosphere.q: Consider the following statements on salinity by students. (A) 'Water is equally salty across the world's oceans'. (B) 'Salinity increases with depth'.'(C) 'Salinity increases on the surface also because of evaporation'. Arrange the understanding level of the students on the topic starting from the one who is least clear.
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Statement (A) : This is completely incorrect. 
Salinity varies across ocean due to factors like 
evaporation, rainfall, river inflow and ice melting. It 
reflects the least understanding of the concept. 
Statement (B) : This is partially true. In some ocean 
regions, salinity may increase with depth, but not 
uniformly. It shows a moderate level of understanding. 
Statement (C) : This is scientifically accurate. High 
evaporation in hot regions increases surface salinity. It 
reflects the clearest understanding. 
Thus, the correct order from least to most clear 
understanding is (A), (B), (C).

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following instruments measures the salinity of sea water?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
A salinometer is the primary instrument used 
to measure the salinity of sea water. It is device 
specifically designed to measure the dissolved salt 
content in a solution.

Hydrosphere.q: The regular rise and fall of ocean waters is known as-
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The regular rise and fall of ocean water is 
known as tides. These are caused by the combined 
gravitational pull of the Moon and sun on the earth.

Hydrosphere.q: Higher salinity is recorded in the North Sea due to which one of the following?
options: Due to influx of river waters in large quantity.
Vapor of more saline water brought by the North Allantic Drift.
Due to influx of melted water from the Arctic ocean.
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The North sea exhibits high salinity primarily 
due of the influence of the North Atlantic Drift, a warm 
ocean current which brings in more saline water from 
the Atlantic Ocean.

Hydrosphere.q: Which one of the followings is the average temperature of the earth at sea-level?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The average temperature of the earth at sea level 
is generally considered to be around 15°C (59°F). 
The option 15.2°C is the closest accurate approximation.

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following salts is present in highest percentage in ocean water?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The salt present in the highest percentage in 
ocean water is Sodium Chloride (NaCl), also known as 
table salt. 1 liter of ocean water contains about 35grams 
of dissolved salts with Sodium Chloride (NaCl) being 
the predominant component.

Hydrosphere.q: The status of salinity in Indian Ocean (in northern summer) is given below. Identify the correct statements. A The salinity in the Indian Ocean increases from equator to the Bay of Bengal. B The salinity in the Indian Ocean decreases from equator towards the Bay of Bengal. C The salinity in the Indian Ocean remains same in different parts. D The 45% isohaline the divide the Indian Ocean into eastern and western section. E Salinity is more in the Arabian Sea than the Bay of Bengal. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Generally, the salinity in the Indian Ocean 
decreases as you move from the equatorial regions 
towards the Bay of Bengal. This primarily due to the 
influx of freshwater from rivers like the Ganges and the 
significant rainfall, especially during the monsoon 
season, which dillites the ocean water in the Bay of 
Bengal. 
• The Arabian sea generally has higher salinity than the 
Bay of Bengal. This happen due to a combination of 
factors, including higher evaporation rates and lower 
freshwater influx in the Arabian sea compared to the 
Bay of Bengal.

Hydrosphere.q: Arrange the following seas in ascending order of concentration of salinity (minimum to maximum) A Red Sea B China Sea C Baltic Sea D Black Sea Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
Hydrosphere.explanation:
In ascending order of salinity (minimum to 
maximum), the seas are typically : Baltic sea, Black sea, 
china sea & Red sea.

Hydrosphere.q: The density of oceanic water is generally lowest in______.
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The density of oceanic water is generally 
lowest in the equatorial regions. This is due to the 
combination of higher surface temperatures and lower 
salinity caused by high precipitation rates in these areas. 
Hydrosphere 342

Hydrosphere.q: Which one the following represents average temperature of water at bottom in the Red sea?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The average temperature of the water at the 
bottom of the Red sea is around 21°C to 22°C. This 
temperature remains relatively stable throughout the 
water column, contrasting with duper areas in the Gulf 
of Aden, where temperatures decrease significantly with 
depth.

Hydrosphere.q: 'Thermocline layer' in a temperature-depth profile of an ocean is characterised by
options: Rapid decrease in temperature with increasing depth
Rapid increase in temperature with increasing depth
Hydrosphere.explanation:
'Thermocline layer' in a temperature-depth 
profile of an ocean is characterized by rapid decrease in 
temperature with increasing depth. It's the transition 
zone between the warmer, mixed surface water and the 
colder, deeper water. This layer essentially acts as a 
barrier, hindering the mixing of surface and deep ocean 
waters.

Hydrosphere.q: Choose the correct sequence of words in the given options to complete the sentence given below The enclosed seas in the ________ latitudes record relatively ________ temperature than the open seas A. Low, lower B. Low, higher C. High, lower D. High, higher
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The enclosed seas in the low latitudes record 
relatively higher than the open seas. This because 
enclosed seas have limited exchange with the open 
ocean, leading to a slower response to seasonal 
temperature changes and a tendency to became colder 
more rapidly.

Hydrosphere.q: Which one of the following salinities represents for Great Salt Lake?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The salinity of the Great Salt Lake is a key 
characteristic, varying considerably between different 
ports of the lake. Gilbert Bay, the main basin, typically 
ranges from 5 to 27% (50 to 270 parts per thousand). 
• The lake salinity varies with the lake's level, 
influenced by evaporation and the addition of salt from 
rivers and stream. The high salinity of the GSL is due to 
its being a closed basin, meaning water can only lave 
through evaporation, leaving salts behind.

Hydrosphere.q: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the percentage of salts found in sea water in decreasing order?
options: Sodium chloride, magnesium chloride, magnesium sulphate, calcium sulphate
Sodium chloride, magnesium sulphate, calcium sulphate, magnesium chloride
Sodium chloride, calcium sulphate, magnesium chloride, magnesium sulphate
Magnesium chloride, sodium chloride, magnesium sulphate, calcium sulphate
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The correct percentage sequences of salt

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following data are sources of proxy data for climate change studies? (A) Historical documents (B) Sea floor sediments (C) Satellite data (D) Fossil pollen.Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A and C Only (c) A, B and D Only
B and C Only (d) C and D Only
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Proxy data are indirect sources used to study 
past climate conditions before the advent of modern 
instruments. 
Among the given options: 
(A) Historical documents 
(B) Sea floor sediments 
(D) Fossil Pollen 
However, satellite data (c) are not proxy data they are

Hydrosphere.q: What affects subsurface ocean circulation among the following?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Subsurface ocean circulation is affected by 
both temperature and salinity. 
The factors that influence the amount of salinity in 
oceans, seas, and lakes are called "controlling factors." 
These include evaporation, precipitation, river inflow, 
wind, ocean currents, and waves.

Hydrosphere.q: When does the salinity of ocean water decrease?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Heavy rainfall decreases the salinity of ocean 
water. 
The salinity of oceans, seas, and lakes is influenced by 
evaporation, precipitation, river inflow, wind, ocean 
currents, and waves.

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following is extensively absorbed by the sea surface?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Long-wave radiation is absorbed by the sea 
surface. 
Visible wave radiation is visible to the eyes and is 
suitable for remote sensing using film and photo 
sensors. 
Mid-wave radiation is the longest wavelength region in 
the electromagnetic spectrum and is used for remote 
sensing and weather monitoring. 
Ultraviolet wave radiation is absorbed by ozone in the 
atmosphere.

Hydrosphere.q: Which one of the following statements is false?
options: The average salinity in the Northern Hemisphere is lower than in the Southern Hemisphere.
The Gulf Stream increases salinity on the northwestern coast of Europe.
The eastern part of the Mediterranean Sea has higher salinity than the western part.
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Anticyclonic conditions increase salinity, not 
decrease it. 
The average ocean salinity is 35 ppt. 
In the Northern Hemisphere, the average salinity is 34 
ppt, while in the Southern Hemisphere, it is 35 ppt. 
The Gulf Stream increases salinity on the northwestern 
coast of Europe due to evaporation. 
The eastern Mediterranean Sea has higher salinity than 
the western part.

Hydrosphere.q: Which one of the following statements is true?
options: The Benguela Current is a cold current in the Pacific Ocean.
The highest oceanic salinity is found between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn.
When the Sun, Moon, and Earth align, a neap tide occurs.
High sea tides occur every 12 hours and 20 minutes.
Hydrosphere.explanation:
The highest oceanic salinity is found between 
the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn. 
The highest salinity is observed between 20°-40° N 
latitude and 10°-30° S latitude. 
Salinity decreases between 40°-60° latitude in both 
hemispheres. 
The Benguela Current is a cold current in the South 
Atlantic Ocean, not the Pacific. 
When the Sun, Moon, and Earth align, a spring tide 
occurs, not a neap tide. 
High tides occur approximately every 12 hours and 26 
minutes, not 12 hours and 20 minutes. 
Note: The highest salinity levels in the world are found in 
Van Lake (Turkey) – 330 ppt 
Dead Sea – 238 ppt 
Great Salt Lake (USA) – 220 ppt

Hydrosphere.q: Assertion (A): The oceans in the Northern Hemisphere record relatively higher average temperatures than those in the Southern Hemisphere. Reason (R): The temperature difference between the Northern and Southern Hemispheres is due to the uneven distribution of land and oceans. Choose the correct answer:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) correctly explains (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) does not correctly explain (A).
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) correctly 
explains (A). 
Oceans in the Northern Hemisphere have higher 
average temperatures than those in the Southern 
Hemisphere due to the unequal distribution of land and 
water.

17.2°C. 
• In the Southern Hemisphere, oceanic isotherms 
follow latitude lines. 
• The highest temperatures are found near the Tropic 
of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn.

Hydrosphere.q: The evaporation process in ocean water is affected by: (a) Salinity (b) Latitude (c) Weather (d) Wind Choose the most appropriate answer: (a) Only (a) and (b) (b) Only (b) and (c) (c) Only (b), (c), and (d) (d) All
Hydrosphere.explanation:
All (a), (b), (c), and (d) 
Evaporation in oceans, seas, and lakes is influenced by 
salinity, rainfall, solar radiation, latitude, wind, and 
ocean currents.

Hydrosphere.q: Which of the following statements about seawater are correct? (a) The density of seawater depends on temperature, pressure, and salinity. (b) Water convergence has no effect on density. (c) Thermal expansion of water changes with temperature fluctuations. (d) Due to excessive rainfall in mid-latitudes, density increases. Select the correct answer: (a) Only
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Only (a) and (c) are correct. 
Water convergence affects density (so statement (b) is 
false). 
In mid-latitudes, high rainfall causes a decrease in 
density, not an increase. 
Density is influenced by temperature, pressure, and 
salinity: 
Temperature → Thermal expansion 
Pressure → Compressibility 
Salinity → Dissolved elements 
Pure water density = 1.000 g/cm³ (at 4°C) 
Average ocean water density = 1.0278 g/cm³, 2-3% 
higher than pure water.

Hydrosphere.q: In which of the following water bodies is the lowest salinity found?
Hydrosphere.explanation:
Karabugas Bay has the lowest salinity, with a 
salinity level of 17‰. The Great Salt Lake in the United 
States has a salinity of 220‰, the Dead Sea has 238‰, 
and Turkey’s Van Lake has 330‰. The average salinity 
of oceans is 35‰. Near the equator, salinity is around 
34.85‰, while the highest salinity (36‰) is found 
between 20°-40° North latitude.
