Indian Geography.q: How many Flinn-Engdahl seismic regions are there in the world based on political and geographical boundaries and seismic activity?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The world is divided into 754 Flinn-Engdahl 
seismic regions, based on political and geographical 
boundaries as well as seismic activity. The Flinn
Engdahl seismic regions were proposed in 1965 by 
Edward A. Flinn and E.R. Engdahl. 
Indian Geography 704

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following regions does not fall under the arid region?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Andaman & Nicobar Islands do not fall 
under the arid region, whereas Central Maharashtra, 
Western Rajasthan, and Haryana are part of the arid 
region.

Indian Geography.q: The Nine Degree Channel is located between –
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Nine Degree Channel (9°) is located 
between Kavaratti (Lakshadweep) and Minicoy. The 
8° Channel separates the Maldives and Minicoy, while 
the 10° Channel separates Little Andaman and Car 
Nicobar.

Indian Geography.q: Which is the largest river island in India?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Majuli is the largest raverine island is 
Assam. It is located in the Brahmputra river, and in 
2016, it became the first raverine island to be made a 
district in India.

Indian Geography.q: Total area of Jharkhand.
Indian Geography.explanation:
Jharkhand's total geographical area is 79.70 
lakh hectares, which is 2.42% of India's total area. It 
ranks 15th in size among the Indian states.

Indian Geography.q: If India were located 200 km further south, which of the following would be its main feature?
Indian Geography.explanation:
If India were situated further south, it would 
be closer to the equatorial climate, which is 
characterized by tropical evergreen forests.

Indian Geography.q: Which Indian Union Territory has three separate districts in three different states?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Puducherry is the only Union Territory with 
three districts in different states: Mahe (Kerala), 
Yanam (Andhra Pradesh), and Karaikal & Puducherry 
(Tamil Nadu).

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following indicates the southernmost point of India?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Indira Point is the southernmost point of 
India. It is located south of the Andaman and Nicobar 
Islands, at 6°4' N latitude. The mainland of India starts 
from 8°4' N latitude. This is why Indira Point is 
considered the southernmost point of India. This island 
is under India's control.

Indian Geography.q: The southern boundary of mainland India is at:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The southern boundary of mainland India is 
at 8°4' N latitude, while including the islands, the 
southernmost boundary is at 6°4' N latitude at Indira 
Point.

Indian Geography.q: Among the four major cities of India, the least temperature variation is observed in:
Indian Geography.explanation:
In Mumbai, the maximum temperature in 
January is 22.5°C, while in July, it rises to 27.5°C. In 
Chennai, the maximum temperature in January is also 
22.5°C, but in July, it rises to 30°C. Hyderabad, 
located on the Deccan Plateau, experiences a greater 
temperature variation due to continentality, making its 
variation higher than that of Mumbai.

Indian Geography.explanation:
Mahabaleshwar is located in Satara 
district, Maharashtra. It is a hill station in southwest 
Maharashtra, offering a picturesque view of the coastal 
Konkan region.

Indian Geography.q: The McMahon Line separates which two countries?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The McMahon Line separates India and 
China. It was named after British official Henry 
McMahon and was defined in the Shimla Agreement. 
The border between India and Pakistan is marked by 
the Radcliffe Line.

Indian Geography.q: Where does the Sun never appear directly overhead?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Allahabad lies north of the Tropic of 
Cancer, so the Sun never appears directly overhead 
there. Ahmedabad, Jabalpur, Kolkata, and Ranchi are 
closer to the Tropic of Cancer, so they experience the 
Sun almost directly overhead at certain times of the 
year.

Indian Geography.q: In terms of area, India's rank in the world is:
Indian Geography.explanation:
India is the 7th largest country in the world 
by area, covering 2.4% of the Earth's land surface. The 
six countries larger than India are- Russia, Canada, 
China, the United States, Brazil, and Australia. India 
stretches 3,214 km north to south and 2,933 km east to 
west.

Indian Geography.q: The tribal population of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands belongs to:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The indigenous population of the Andaman 
and Nicobar Islands belongs to the Negroid race. 
These are among the oldest human races and are now 
found in limited numbers in Congo Basin (Africa), 
Sri Lanka, Malaysia, and the Andaman Islands.

Indian Geography.q: The Silent Valley Movement is related to:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Silent Valley Movement was a social 
movement aimed at conserving the Silent Valley, an 
evergreen tropical forest in the Palakkad district of 
Kerala, India. In 1985, the area was declared as the 
Silent Valley National Park. The Silent Valley in 
Kerala covers a biological rich area of 89 km².

Indian Geography.q: The highest potential for tidal energy production in India is in:
Indian Geography.explanation:
Tides, ocean currents, and waves are major 
sources of oceanic energy. Electricity is generated 
using turbines operated by tidal rise and fall. In India, 
the Gulf of Khambhat, the Gulf of Kutch, and the 
Hooghly estuary are suitable locations for tidal energy 
production, with a potential of 1000 MW.

Indian Geography.q: Where are the Tapovan and Vishnugad Hydroelectric Projects located?

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the cities of Patna (Bihar) and Kolkata (West Bengal)?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The term "Primate City" is appropriate for 
Patna and Kolkata. 
• The largest city of a vast region, which leads and 
represents the entire region due to its size, is called 
the Primary City. 
• Mark Jefferson introduced the term "Primate City."

Indian Geography.q: Which area in the Indian subcontinent is frequently affected by tropical cyclones?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Tropical cyclones form in intertropical 
regions (30° N latitude – 30° S latitude). These are 
low-pressure convergent circulation systems with an 
average diameter of up to 640 km. The direction of air 
circulation in the Northern Hemisphere is 
counterclockwise, while in the Southern Hemisphere, 
it is clockwise. These cyclones often cause severe 
devastation along the Coromandel Coast (Odisha, 
West Bengal, and Andhra Pradesh).

Indian Geography.q: The total area of India is:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The total area of India is 3,287,263 sq km. 
It is the seventh-largest country in the world (2.43% of 
the world's land area). Only Russia, Canada, China, the 
United States, Brazil, and Australia are larger than India.

Indian Geography.explanation:

Indian Geography.q: During which Five-Year Plan was the Bhoodan Movement initiated?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Bhoodan Movement was started by 
Acharya Vinoba Bhave in 1951. It was a voluntary land 
reform movement. After independence, the economic 
disparity caused by unequal landholdings led to severe 
distress among farmers. Vinoba Bhave inspired landlords 
to voluntarily donate land to the landless. The movement 
began in Pochampally village, Telangana.

Indian Geography.q: In which year was the McMahon Line demarcated?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Several international borders have been 
subjects of historical disputes. The McMahon Line was 
demarcated in 1914 under an agreement by Sir Henry 
McMahon (British India) to define the border between 
India and China. However, China has periodically 
refused to recognize this boundary. 
Indian Geography 708

Indian Geography.q: The territorial dispute over Gilgit-Baltistan is between which countries?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The territorial dispute over Gilgit-Baltistan 
exists between India and Pakistan. The conflict is also 
related to the Siachen Glacier, a geopolitical issue in 
Jammu and Kashmir. In 1984, Pakistan permitted around 
70 foreign mountaineers to ski near the Khunjerab Pass, 
which led to Indian objections and escalated tensions.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following caves is not in Maharashtra?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Ajanta, Ellora, and Elephanta Caves are 
located in Maharashtra. The Ellora and Elephanta 
Caves were built during the Rashtrakuta period. Ellora 
consists of 34 rock-cut caves—1 to 12 are Buddhist, 13 
to 29 are Hindu, and 30 to 34 are Jain. However, the 
Amarnath Cave is in Jammu and Kashmir.

Indian Geography.q: Which island lies between India and Sri Lanka?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Rameswaram Island is located between 
India and Sri Lanka, near Dhanushkodi, and separates 
the Jaffna Peninsula from the Indian mainland. 
Lakshadweep is located in the Arabian Sea, New 
Moore Island is in the Bay of Bengal, and Elephanta 
Island is near Mumbai, Maharashtra.

Indian Geography.q: Where are topographical maps and survey sheets of India published?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Survey of India, headquartered in 
Dehradun, publishes topographical maps and survey 
sheets. Atlases are published from Kolkata.

Indian Geography.q: What is the total length of India’s coastline?
Indian Geography.explanation:
India’s length from east to west is 2,933 km, 
and from north to south is 3,214 km. The land 
boundary is 15,200 km, while the total coastal 
boundary, including islands, is 7,516.6 km. The 
mainland coastline is about 6,100 km.

Indian Geography.q: If the Equator had passed through India instead of the Tropic of Cancer, what would have been the climatic impact?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Tropic of Cancer passes through the 
middle of India. If the Equator had passed through, 
India, the country would have experienced an 
equatorial climate with consistently high temperatures 
and heavy rainfall throughout the year.

Indian Geography.q: India’s longitudinal extent is from 68°7' E to 97°25' E. What is its latitudinal extent?
Indian Geography.explanation:
India's shape is not strictly triangular, but 
rather more quadrilateral. The Ancient geographer 
Strabo described its shape as kite-like. The mainland 
of India lies entirely in the Northern Hemisphere, 
extending from 8°4' N to 37°6' N latitude and 68°7' E 
to 97°25' E longitude.

Indian Geography.q: Which is the largest bay in India?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The largest bay in India is the Bay of Bengal, 
located in the northeastern part of the Indian ocean.

Indian Geography.q: On which river is Jabalpur city located?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Jabalpur city is situated on the banks of the 
Narmada River. The river originates from the western 
region of Amarkantak and flows through a rift valley 
between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges before 
draining into the Arabian Sea. The famous Dhuandhar 
Falls is a major attraction near Jabalpur.

Maitri, and the latest is Bharati.

Indian Geography.explanation:
The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are

submerged mountain ranges.

Indian Geography.q: Which city recently completed 300 years of its existence?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Kolkata recently completed 300 years. 
Located on the eastern bank of the Hooghly River, it is 
also know as the 'Gateway to Eastern India.'

Indian Geography.q: Where was India's first telephone service launched?
Indian Geography.explanation:
India’s first telephone service was launched 
in Kolkata. The Oriental Telephone Company of 
England set up exchanges in Kolkata, Bombay, 
Madras (Chennai), and Ahmedabad in 1881. Formal 
telephone services began on 28 January 1882, with 93 
subscribers.

Indian Geography.q: Who was the first traveler to discover India?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Vasco da Gama reached India in 1498 via 
the Cape of Good Hope and the Indian Ocean. He met 
the local ruler, the Zamorin of Calicut. Christopher 
Columbus discovered America in 1492.

Indian Geography.q: Statement (A): Bihar is a backward state in India. Reason (R): There is regional disparity in the development levels within Bihar. Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) explains (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) does not explain (A).
Indian Geography.explanation:
Bihar is considered a backward state due to 
low literacy rates and poverty levels, but certain 
areas are developing. Hence, both the statement and 
reason are correct and explain each other.

Indian Geography.q: Assertion (A): The Dandakaranya region was the first major inter-state effort for refugee resettlement. Reason (R): The Dandakaranya region is partly in Bihar and partly in West Bengal. Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) explains (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) does not explain (A).
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Dandakaranya region was a major 
inter-state effort for the resettlement of Bangladeshi 
refugees. However, it does not include Bihar or 
West Bengal, but Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and 
Andhra Pradesh.

Indian Geography.q: Which Indian island has a volcanic origin?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Barren Island, located north of Port Blair, 
is India's only active volcano, along with Narcondam 
Island (a dormant volcano).

Indian Geography.q: Assertion (A): Northern plains and the eastern coastal regions of India have a dense railway network. Reason (R): These regions have well-developed industries. Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) explains (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) does not explain (A).
Indian Geography.explanation:
The northern plains (UP, Bihar, Punjab, 
Haryana) and the eastern coastal regions have a 
dense railway network due to flat terrain and high 
population density, but industrial development is not 
the primary reason.

Indian Geography.q: Arrange the following states on the basis of their total area in ascending order: A. Uttarakhand B. Jharkhand C. Telengana D. Chhattisgarh Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
Indian Geography.explanation:
States arranged in the correct ascending order 
based on their total area are – Uttarakhand → Jharkhand 
→ Telangana → Chhattisgarh. 
• Uttarakhand has an area of 53,483 sq. km. Its capital 
is Dehradun. Due to its holy places and pilgrimage 
sites, it is often called the land of gods/‘Dev 
Bhoomi’. 
• Jharkhand has an area of 79,714 sq. km. It came into 
existence in November 2000 as a state of the Union. 
It is very rich in mineral resources. 
• Telangana became a new state in 2014 after 
separating from Andhra Pradesh. Its area is 112,077 
sq. km. It is located on the Deccan Plateau in the 
central section of the eastern peninsular coast of 
India. 
• Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh in 
November 2000. Its area is 135,194 sq. km. 
Therefore, option (a) is correct.

Indian Geography.q: _______ in the Indian ocean is a ‘Miniature India.’
Indian Geography.explanation:
Mauritius, located in the Indian Ocean, is 
called “Little India.” Mauritius is an equatorial island 
nation. It is referred to as “Little India” because a large 
proportion of its population is of Indian origin, brought 
to Mauritius from India during the British colonial 
period. There are significant similarities between the 
two countries in terms of culture, traditions, language, 
religion, as well as political and cultural relations.

Indian Geography.q: The boundaries that do not follow the spatial distribution of cultural groups or political cultures are called :
Indian Geography.explanation:
Boundaries that do not follow the spatial 
distribution of cultural groups or political cultures are 
called superimposed boundaries. Superimposed 
boundaries are determined after the development of 
cultural landscapes corresponding to subsequent 
boundaries, but in their determination, the cultural and 
ethnic features of the region are ignored. In such cases, 
it is difficult to consider the unique cultural and ethnic 
characteristics of a region, because the boundaries are 
defined, drawn, and imposed by external powers as a 
result of conflicting forces and ceasefire agreements, 
rather than based on local needs. Antecedent 
boundaries, on the other hand, are those formed and 
defined before the development of present cultural 
patterns. Such boundaries developed in the New World 
countries as rival colonial powers expanded their 
influence and reached agreements.

mineral resources.

the Persian Gulf, Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, and along 
the western coast of Australia.

Indian Geography.q: In which ocean is the island of Diego Garcia located?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Diego Garcia is located in the Indian Ocean. 
It was discovered in 1500 by Portuguese explorer 
Diego Garcia, after whom the island was named. 
Between 1814 and 1965, it was part of Mauritius but 
later came under British control. In 1976, Britain 
leased it to the United States, which established air 
and naval bases there during the Cold War. Today, 
both the U.S. and the U.K. have military bases on 
the island.

Indian Geography.q: Which is the largest island in the Indian Ocean?
Indian Geography.explanation:

Madagascar, with an area of 590,000 square 
kilometers, while Sumatra has an area of 473,600 
square kilometers, and Lakshadweep covers only 32 
square kilometers. The largest island in the region is 
Borneo, shared by Brunei, Indonesia, and Malaysia.

Indian Geography.q: Assertion (A): Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh are ideal states for wheat production in India. Reason (R): These states have well-drained fertile soil, sowing temperatures of 10°C to 15°C, and annual rainfall of around 75 cm. Choose the correct option:

explains (A), the correct answer is (a).

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following is the oldest Indian rock system?

“most ancient” or related to the earliest geological age 
of the Earth. Two sequences of Archean rocks are 
found: 
(a) Archean Granite and Gneiss, and 
(b) Dharwar Sediments. 
The geological history of India begins with these most 
ancient rocks.

Kerala coast in the south, can be divided into the 
following parts – Kachchh and Kathiawar coast of 
Gujarat, the Konkan and Goa coast of Maharashtra, and 
the Malabar coast of Karnataka and Kerala respectively.

as the “Coromandel Coast.”

Indian Geography.q: Arrange the following from South to North Sequence. I. Pirpnajal range II. Zanskar range III. Greater Himalayas IV. Ladakh range Select the correct answer from the code given below:
options: II, III, IV, I UP Higher 16/04/2025
Indian Geography.explanation:
The sequence of mountain ranges from south 
to north is as follows: Pir Panjal Range → Greater 
Himalaya → Zaskar Range → Ladakh Range. 
Longitudinally, the Himalayas consist of three parallel 
ranges and a trans-Himalayan region from south to 
north. Their sequence is as follows: 
(i) Sub-Himalaya or Shiwalik, 
(ii) Lesser Himalaya or Himachal, 
(iii) Greater Himalaya or Himadri, 
(iv) Trans-Himalaya or Tethys Himalaya. 
The Pir Panjal range is the major range of the Lesser 
Himalayas. It extends for about 400 km between the 
Jhelum and Beas rivers. To the northwest of the Greater 
Himalaya lies the Zaskar range, to the north of which 
flows the Indus River. The Karakoram, Ladakh, and 
Kailash ranges are included in the Trans-Himalaya or 
Tethys Himalaya

Indian Geography.q: Arrange the following west flowing rivers in peninsular India from North to South. I. Sabarmati II. Tapi III. Kali Nadi IV. Bharathappuzha Select the correct answer from the code given below.

Indian Geography.explanation:
The west-flowing rivers of Peninsular India 
arranged from north to south are: Sabarmati, Tapi, Kali 
River, and Bharathapuzha. 
• The Sabarmati is a west-flowing river originating 
from the Mewar Hills (Aravallis) and draining into 
the Gulf of Khambhat. Its length is 371 km. 
• The Tapi is the second major west-flowing river, 
originating from Multai in Betul district, Madhya 
Pradesh, from the Satpura ranges. Its length is 724 
km. The Purna is its main tributary, joining near 
Bhusawal. The Kakrapara and Ukai projects are 
located on this river. 
• The Kali River originates from Diggi village in 
Uttara Kannada district of Karnataka and joins the 
Arabian Sea near Karwar. 
• The Bharathapuzha is an important west-flowing 
river of Kerala.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following mountain ranges of Peninsular India has the highest peak ?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The highest peak of Peninsular India is 
Anamudi (2695 m), located in the Anamalai Hills of the 
Western Ghats. The Western Ghats extend for about 
1600 km, from the Tapi River in the north to Cape 
Comorin (Kanyakumari) in the south. The Vindhyan 
range separates the vast northern plains from the rest of 
Peninsular India. It stretches for about 1050 km from 
Jobat in Gujarat to Sasaram in Bihar. The Aravalli range 
extends for about 800 km in a northeast–southwest 
direction between Delhi and Palanpur (Gujarat). Its 
highest peak is Guru Shikhar (1722 m), located at 
Mount Abu. The Satpura range extends about 900 km 
from Ratnapur in the west to Amarkantak in the east. Its 
highest peak is Dhoopgarh (1350 m), located in the 
Mahadeo Hills.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rivers flow through antecedent valleys?
options: More than one of the above
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Sutlej and Indus rivers flow through 
antecedent valleys. Rivers that maintain their original 
course even after the uplift of landmass are called 
antecedent (superimposed/precedent) rivers, and the 
valleys formed by them are called antecedent valleys. 
Most of the major Himalayan rivers such as the Indus, 
Sutlej, Ghaghra, Kali, Gandak, Tista, and Brahmaputra 
are examples of antecedent rivers. The collective system 
of such rivers is known as the antecedent drainage 
system.

Indian Geography.q: What is the name of the mountain range in India that separates the Indo-Gangetic Plain from the Deccan Plateau?
options: More than one of the above
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Vindhya mountain range separates the 
Indo-Gangetic plain from the Deccan Plateau. Along 
with the Satpura range, it forms the watershed of central 
India, where rivers like the Narmada, Chambal, Betwa, 
Tons, Ken, and Son originate. Some of these flow 
toward the Ganges, while others flow toward the 
Godavari and Mahanadi. The Indo-Gangetic plain 
stretches 3,200 km east to west, with an average width 
of 150–300 km. The Deccan Plateau is bounded by the 
Western Ghats in the west, the Eastern Ghats in the east, 
and the Satpura, Maikal, and Mahadev hills in the north.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following ranges are called Daffla, Miri, Abor and Mishmi in Arunachal Pradesh?

and Andhra Pradesh into the Bay of Bengal.

Indian Geography.explanation:

Himalayas are primarily composed of metamorphic

Indian Geography.q: Which one of the following states of India is known as 'Molasses Basin'?
Indian Geography.explanation:

Indian Geography.q: River Indus flows between which of the following mountain ranges:
Indian Geography.explanation:

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following statements are true about the Drainage System of the rivers? (A) The drainage pattern resembling the branches of a tree is known as 'dendritic'. (B) The drainage pattern of the rivers originating from hill is known as 'radial'. (C) When the primary tributaries of rivers flow parallel to each other and secondary tributaries join them at right angles, the pattern is known as 'centripetal'. (D) When the rivers discharge their waters from all directions in a lake or depression, the pattern is known as 'trellis'.
Indian Geography.explanation:
(A) Dendritic pattern: 
Appearance - Look like the branches of a tree. 
Formation- forms in regions where the rock structures 
is uniform and there are no significant controls. 
(B) Radial Pattern- 
Appearance - Rivers flow outward in all directions from 
a central high point. 
Formation - Usually found on domes, volcanic cones, or 
high mountains. 
(C) Centripetal pattern - Rivers flow inward from 
different dissections to ward a central low-lying basin 
Formation - found in basis or depressions. 
(D) Trellis Pattern - main river flows in a straight line 
and tributaries join it at right angles 
Formation - Occur in areas with alternating bonds of 
hard and soft rock usually in folded or faulted regions.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following states is the largest producer of Iron ore in India?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Odisha contributes around 54% of India's 
total Iron ore production making it the top producer in 
the country. Major mining areas in Odisha include 
Mayurbhanj, Sundergarh and Keonjhar.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rivers is not an East flowing river?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Mahi River is one of the few rivers in 
India that flow westward. It originates in Madhya

Indian Geography.q: In which of the Agro-Climatic sub zones of Rajasthan does the Hadauti Plateau lie?
Indian Geography.explanation:

Indian Geography.q: Read the following statements about Himalaya Rivers and choose the correct answer from given options. (i) Himalayan rivers are perennial. (ii) Himalayan rivers recieve water from rain and snow. (iii) Himalayan rivers form meanders in their upper course. (iv) Himalayan rivers have well development deltas. Select the correct answer from the codes given below: Code:
Indian Geography.explanation:
Himalayas rivers are perennial because they 
are fed by both glacial melt and rainfall throughout the 
year. 
• In their upper course, Himalayas rivers flow rapidly 
due to steep slopes and do not form meanders. 
Meanders usually form in the middle and lower 
course where the land is flatter. 
• Himalayan rivers like the Ganga and Brahmaputra 
form well developed deltas.

Indian Geography.q: Read the following statements about Brahmaputra River and choose the correct answer from given option. Statement (I) : In Tibet, the river carries high volume of water and high silt. Statement (II) : In India, it passes through a region of high rainfall.

carries a low volume of water and very little silt in 
Tibet. 
Statement-II is true- In India, the Brahmaputra flows 
through regions like Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, 
which receive very high rainfall; As a result, the river 
swells and carries a large volume of water and silt.

Indian Geography.explanation:

Indian Geography.q: Most of the river valley projects constructed to control floods failed and instead triggered floods because of
options: heavy rain led water released from dam
extensive soil erosion due to flood
More than one of the above
Indian Geography.explanation:
Most river valley projects were constructed for 
flood prevention, but instead, they worsened thee flood 
situation. This happened because excessive sediment 
accumulated in their reservoirs. When there is too much 
sediment, the water released from the dam can lead to 
flooding. Additionally, due to heavy rainfall, it becomes 
necessary to release water from the dam, which also 
causes floods. These floods result in large-scale soil 
erosion. 
Note : According to the provisional answer key released 
by BPSC, the correct answer to this question has been 
marked as option (e), which is incorrect. The correct 
answer should be option (d).

Indian Geography.q: Which one of the following is NOT an objective of Namami Gange?

rainfall and steep slopes are highly vulnerable to 
landslides. The combination of heavy rainfall and steep

land slides. Therefore, these areas are classified as "very

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following states is the most affected by flood?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Assam is among the most flood-affected

significant damage to life, property and agriculture.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rivers is known as "Sorrow of Bihar"?

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of peninsular river system?
Indian Geography.explanation:

Himalayan rivers, where rivers existed before the land

Indus, Brahmaputra) 
• Peninsular rivers are mostly formed after the land was 
uplifted and generally follow the slope of the land 
(consequent drainage), not antecedent.

Indian Geography.q: According to Indira Gandhi Canal Department (Government of Rajasthan), what is the approximate length of total lift canals (according to July, 2022)?
Indian Geography.explanation:
According to the Indira Gandhi canal 
department (Government of Rajasthan), the total length 
of lift canals (as of July, 2022) is 1495.45 km. Indira 
Gandhi (Rajasthan) canal project is the world's largest 
irrigation project which will transform the economy of 
the arid and semi-arid areas of Rajasthan.

Indian Geography.q: The area famous for its 'Duar formations' is -
Indian Geography.explanation:
Over means 'duar' or 'gateway' as these plains 
act as entry points to Bhutan and eastern Himalayas. 
• Duars are located in the foothills of the eastern 
Himalayas particularly in northern west Bengal and 
parts of the Sikkim Himalaya region. 
• They are alluvial flood plains formed by rivers 
flowing down from the Himalayas. Such as Teesta, 
Tarsa and Jaldhaka. Duars are divided into two 
parts- 
• Eastern duars (mainly in Assam) 
• Western duars (mainly ins West Bengal and Sikkim) 
• The region receives heavy rainfall, making it ideal 
for tea cultivation and dense forests. 
• Duars are home to rich wildlife and several national 
parks and wildlife sanctuaries like Jaldapara and 
Gorumara. 
• The region is strategically important due to its 
proximity to Bhutan and China and serves as a key 
corridor for trade and military access.

Indian Geography.explanation:

 Banas Menal

 Luni Sagi 
 Sabarimati Wakal 
Parvati river is a tributary of Chambal river and also a 
tributary of Yamuna. Chambal river originates near 
mhow (600 m) situated an Malwa plateau of Madhya 
Pradesh. kali, Sindh, Sipta, Parvati and Banas are its 
major tributaries. 
• Luni tributaries include Sagi, Sarswati, Bundi, Sukri 
and Jawai etc. 
• Sabarmati's tributaries are Vakal, hathmati Meshwa, 
Majham and Sedhi. 
• Menali or morel is a tributary of Banas.

Indian Geography.q: The Lacustrine and Fluvial depositions in Kashmir Valley are called as:
Indian Geography.explanation:
In the Kashmir Valley Karewa formations are 
lacustrine (lake-origin) and fluvial (river-origin) 
deposits. They are known for their fertile soils and are 
important for growing crops like saffron and almonds.

Indian Geography.q: 'Deccan Trap' is formed through:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The 'Deccan Trap' is one of the largest 
volcanic features on earth. formed around 60 to 68 
million years ago due to massive volcanic eruptions. 
These eruptions released basaltic lava which spread 
over a vast area and solidified into layers of basalt rock. 
The term 'trap' comes from the swedish word 'trappa' 
meaning 'stairs' referring to the step-like landscape 
formed by successive lava flows.

Indian Geography.q: Ten Degree channel separate:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The 10 degree channel is a narrow channel of 
water in the bay of Bengal that separates the little 
Andaman Islands (part of the Andaman Islands) from 
Car Nicobar Island (part of the Nicobar Island). It is 
named after the 10 degree north latitude line which 
passes through it.

Indian Geography.q: Which one of the following is not matched correctly? River Originate place
Indian Geography.explanation:
Jhelum river originates from Verinag spring 
in the Anantnag district of Jammu and Kashmir not 
from Rohtang pass. 
• Sharda (or Kali) river originates form Milam Glacier.

Glacier near lake Mansarovar in Tibet In its upper 
course in Tibet it is known as the Karnali River. 
• Satluj river originates from Rakas Tal near mount

Indian Geography.q: Which one of the following rivers basin is located to the southern most position?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Among the given river basins, the Kaveri 
river basin is located in farthest south India. 
• Kavari river flows through Karnataka and Tamil 
Nadu and reaches the Bay of Bengal. 
• Godavari Tapi and Mahanadi basins are all located 
north of the Kaveri basin.

Indian Geography.q: Which one of the followings is older alluvium in the Gangetic plain?
Indian Geography.explanation:
In the Gangetic plain, Bhangar refers to the 
Oldest alluvium which is found in the slightly elevated 
terraces away from the river floodplains. It is composed 
of older alluvial soil and often contains calcareous 
deposits known Kankar. 
• Khadar is the newer alluvium, deposited by rivers 
annually during floods. 
• Tarai is a marshy region just south of the Bhabar 
zone with high water table and rich in vegetation. 
• Bhabar is a narrow belt of coarse sediment at the 
foothills of the Himalayas.

Indian Geography.q: Which one of the following lengths shows the length of Great Himalayan range from west to east?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Great Himalayas range also known as the 
Himadri, is the highest and northernmost of the three 
major Himalayas ranges. It stretches approximately 
2650 km from Nanga Parbat is in west (Pakistan) to 
Namcha Barwa in Arunachal Pradesh, India (East). 
• It includes the world's highest peaks like Mount 
Everest (8848 m) K2 (8,611 m) and Kanchenjunga 
(8,586 m). 
• The range acts as a natural barrier between the Indian 
subcontinent and the Tibetan Plateau. 
• It is the most continuous and prominent range in the 
Himalayas.

Indian Geography.q: Which one of the followings is the highest peak of Peninsular Plateau?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Anaimudi is the highest peak in the western 
Ghats with an elevation of 2,695 m (8,842 feet) and the 
tallest in Peninsular India, making it the highest point in 
India outside the Himalayan range. It is located in 
Anaimalai Hills, western Ghats, Kerala. 
• Dodabetta - located in the Nilgiri Hills of Tamil 
Nadu, with an elevation of 2,637 m. It is the highest 
peak in the Nilgiris but not in the entire Peninsular 
Plateau. 
• Vavul Mala- Situated in the Vellarimala range of 
Kerala, standing at 2,339 m. It is the highest peak in 
the western Ghats north of the Nilgiris but lower than 
Anaimudi. 
• Makurti/Mukurthi- Situated in the Nilgiri Hills of 
Tamil Nadu, with an elevation of 2,554 m.

Indian Geography.q: Which one of the following rivers joins with Rann of Kucch?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Luni River flows through Rajasthan and 
ends in the marshy lands of the Rann of Kucch in 
Gujarat.

Indian Geography.q: Which one of the followings is the largest east flowing Peninsular river?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Godavari river is the longest east-flowing 
river in peninsular India. It originates in the western 
Ghats at Trimbak in Maharashtra and flows east ward 
across several states before emptying into the Bay of 
Bengal. It is about 1,465 km long making it the second 
longest river in India after the Ganga

Indian Geography.q: Which one of the following peaks is the highest in Indian territory?
Indian Geography.explanation:
India's Himalayan region is incredibly diverse 
and can be broadly categorized into three major 
divisions based on altitude geographic characteristics.

Indian Geography.q: Tungabhadra River is the tributory of which one of the following rivers?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Tungabhadra river is a major tributary of 
the Krishna river . It is farmed by the confluence of the 
Tunga and Bhadra rivers, which originates in the 
western Ghats of Karnataka. 
• The Krishna river is one of the longest rivers in 
peninsular India and the Tungabhadra significantly 
contributes to its water valence, especially in the 
southern part of the Decean plateau.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following region lies in the lowest seismic sensitive zone in India?
Indian Geography.explanation:
India is divided into seismic zones II to V 
(zone II being the least prone to earthquakes and zone V 
the most). 
• Bundelkhand region, located in central India 
(covering parts of Uttar Pradesh and Madhya 
Pradesh) lies mostly in seismic zone II, which is 
considered the least earthquake prone zone in India. 
• Ganga region (likely a reference to the Ganga 
basin) lies in more active zones (III or IV). 
• Konkan region lies near the western coast with 
some moderate activity (zone III). 
• Godavari basin in parts of Andhra Pradesh and 
Maharashtra also falls in zones III and IV.

Indian Geography.explanation:

Brahmaputra river system –

water and silt, heavy deposit of silt has raised the 
river bed. 
• Occassional earthquakes have brought about 
changes in the course of river.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rivers have the largest drainage basin area?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Among the rivers Chambal has the largest 
drainage basin area, covering approximately 132,000 
square kilometers. 
• Narmada covers around 98,800 km2. 
• Kaveri about 81,100 km2 
• Sutlej (in India) about 65,000 km2 
 Although Sutlej is a major river, much of its basin 
lies outside India, so in the center of Indian

basin among the options.

Indian Geography.q: By which other name is the Mandakini River known in Uttarakhand?
Indian Geography.explanation:
In Uttarakhand, the Mandakini River is also 
known as Kali Ganga. This river merges with the 
Alaknanda River in Rudraprayag. The Alaknanda 
River flows and meets the Bhagirathi River at 
Devprayag, after which it continues as the Ganga. The 
Yamuna River joins from the right near Prayag, while 
rivers like Ramganga, Ghaghara, Gandak, and Kosi 
merge from the left. Eventually, the Ganga and 
Brahmaputra combine to form the world's largest delta.

Indian Geography.q: In which region is Pangong Lake located?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Pangong Lake is located in the Eastern 
Ladakh region. In the Ladakhi language, "Pangong" 
means proximity, and in Tibetan, "Tso" means lake. 
The Line of Actual Control (LAC) passes through the 
lake, but India and China have differing views 
regarding its exact position. Some other important 
lakes include:- 
• Jammu & Kashmir: Dal, Wular, Anantnag, 
Nigeen, Berinag 
• Uttarakhand: Nainital, Bhimtal, Khurpatal, 
Roopkund 
• Meghalaya:Umiam 
• Manipur:Loktak 
• Mizoram: Pala

Indian Geography.q: In which of the following regions are Quaternary rock formations NOT found?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Quaternary formations consist of layered 
rocks that developed after the Cuddapah formations 
through water deposition. They cover an area of about 
100,000 square kilometers. They extend from the 
Sasaram and Rohtas regions of Bihar in the east to the 
Chittorgarh region of Rajasthan in the west, and from 
Kashmir in the north to Gujarat in the south.

Indian Geography.q: What is the type of drainage pattern formed in a region where soft and hard rocks are arranged alternately, and streams follow soft rock formations?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The trellis drainage pattern is found in 
areas where hard and soft rock formations are arranged 
in alternating layers. This type of pattern is also found 
in cuesta topography.

Indian Geography.q: Dendritic drainage patterns develop in:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The dendritic drainage pattern resembles 
a tree, with tributaries joining the main river from 
different directions, similar to how small branches 
merge into larger ones. This pattern primarily develops 
in homogeneous and flat regions, such as the Ganga, 
Godavari, and Krishna river basins.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rivers flows through a rift valley?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Tapti River originates near Multai in 
Betul district of Madhya Pradesh, in the Satpura range. 
It flows through a rift valley between the Satpura and 
Ajanta ranges. Its main tributary is the Purna River.

Indian Geography.q: A river valley that develops perpendicular to the general slope of a region is called:
Indian Geography.explanation:
Subsequent valleys develop after 
consequent rivers, following weaker structural 
formations, such as softer rock layers. 
Indian Geography 739

Indian Geography.q: What is a drainage pattern called when it is unrelated to the structural features of the region where it is found?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The superimposed drainage pattern is also 
known as antecedent drainage. This type of drainage 
develops when a river maintains its original course 
regardless of underlying geological structures.

Indian Geography.q: What is the term for a drainage pattern that is not controlled by the original structural formations of a region?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Drainage systems can be divided into two 
main types:

Indian Geography.q: Valleys that continue to flow in the original direction of the consequent drainage but develop at lower topographic levels due to new base levels are called:
Indian Geography.explanation:
Resequent valleys continue flowing in the 
original direction of consequent drainage but develop 
at lower elevations due to changes in base level. 
• Obsequent: Rivers flowing opposite to the main 
consequent river. 
• Subsequent: Rivers that follow weak rock 
structures after the consequent phase. 
• Insequent: Rivers that do not follow geological 
structures.

Indian Geography.q: When a river flows into the main river but moves parallel to the main river in the opposite direction, it represents:
Indian Geography.explanation:
Obsequent rivers flow in the opposite 
direction of the main consequent river. However, they 
still follow the overall slope of the region.

Indian Geography.q: The subsequent drainage generally occurs:
options: In accordance with the consequent drainage
At a right angle to the consequent drainage
Indian Geography.explanation:
The subsequent drainage generally occurs at 
a right angle to the consequent drainage. 
• In any region, the formation of a consequent river 
happens first. Consequent rivers follow the 
regional slope and are also known as dip streams. 
In folded mountainous regions, consequent rivers 
originate in synclinal troughs and are termed 
synclinal consequent rivers.

Indian Geography.q: Valleys whose courses are controlled by factors that cannot be determined are known as—
Indian Geography.explanation:
Rivers that do not follow the regional slope 
but instead flow in an opposite direction, cutting across 
physical structures, are called insequent rivers. The 
insequent drainage system includes antecedent and 
superimposed rivers.

Indian Geography.q: The rivers flowing in the Himalayan region represent which type of drainage system?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The area where the Himalayas exist today 
was once the Tethys Sea, into which rivers flowed 
from the north. However, after the formation of the 
Himalayas during the Tertiary period, these rivers 
began cutting through the mountain range and flowing 
into the Indian subcontinent. As a result, these are 
termed antecedent rivers. The major antecedent rivers 
include the Indus, Sutlej, and Brahmaputra.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rivers flows in the opposite direction to a consequent river?
Indian Geography.explanation:
A river flowing in the opposite direction to 
the principal consequent river is called an obsequent 
river. However, an obsequent river is still a type of 
consequent river because it also follows the slope of 
the land. An obsequent river meets a subsequent river 
at a right angle. 
 
Indian Geography 740

Indian Geography.q: River valleys that initially flow in the same direction as the original consequent drainage but later develop at lower topographic levels in reference to new base levels are known as—
Indian Geography.explanation:
River valleys that initially flow in the same 
direction as the original consequent drainage but later 
develop at lower topographic levels concerning new 
base levels are known as resequent valleys. Drainage 
systems refer to the origin of rivers and their evolution 
over time, whereas drainage patterns refer to the 
geometric arrangement and spatial organization of 
rivers in a given area. 
Drainage systems are classified into two major types:

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following is part of the ‘Eastern Plateau’ geomorphological region of Peninsular India?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Peninsular India is the oldest landmass in 
India. The Bundelkhand Upland is the northernmost 
region, followed southward by the Vindhyan 
Escarpment and the Narmada Valley, with the Garhjat 
Hills located the farthest south. The Bundelkhand 
Upland is the easternmost part of this 
geomorphological region.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rivers flows through a rift valley?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Among the given rivers, the Tapi River 
flows through a rift valley. 
• The Tapi River originates from the Betul plateau 
region in Madhya Pradesh and flows through 
Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat before 
forming an estuary near Surat and emptying into 
the Arabian Sea at the Gulf of Khambhat. 
• Its major tributaries include the Purna, Girna, Bori, 
and Panjhra on the left bank. 
• The Kakrapar Dam and Ukai Project are located on 
this river in Gujarat.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following pairs is incorrectly matched?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Indian rocks are classified into four groups: 
Archaean, Purana, Dravidian, and Aryan. The Purana 
group is further divided into the Cuddapah and Vindhyan 
sequences. The upper Vindhyan sequence includes the 
Bhander series, while the lower sequence is referred to as 
the Semri series (Son River) in Andhra Pradesh as 
Kurnool, and in Rajasthan as the Palni series. The 
Cuddapah sequence includes rock formations such as 
Nallamalai, Cheyyar, and Papaghani series.

Indian Geography.q: Why is salt found in Sambhar?
options: It has a visible deposit of rock salt.
It has a lake with no outward drainage.
It has a lake where seawater enters.
Indian Geography.explanation:
Sambhar Lake in Rajasthan is a closed basin 
where salt is deposited by inflowing water from 
surrounding rocks. Since there is no external drainage, 
the salinity remains high.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rock groups in India is the richest in fossils?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Various rock groups exist in India. 
Cuddapah rocks contain iron ore, manganese, and 
marble. The Vindhyan group consists of sandstone and 
slate. During the Upper Carboniferous period, the 
Indian peninsula underwent tectonic movements, 
forming basins and troughs where numerous land 
plants and animals were buried, eventually forming 
coal deposits. These formations, known as Gondwana 
rocks, are the richest in fossils. The Siwalik range also 
contains a large number of fossilized species.

Indian Geography.q: The Karewas formations in India belong to which geological age?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Karewas formations in India are from the 
Pleistocene Epoch. 
• Karewa term first used by Godwin Austin in 1859. 
• It is thick deposit of unconsolidated lacustrine. 
• Karewas were formed during the Pleistocene period 
when the entire valley of Kashmir under water. 
• It is useful for the cultivation of Zafran (Saffron), 
walnuts, almonds etc. 
Indian Geography 741

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following statements about Himachal Pradesh are correct? (A) High potential for hydroelectric power generation (B) High literacy rate (C) High potential for horticulture activities (D) Abundant mineral resources (E) High proportion of agricultural land Choose the correct option:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The economy of Himachal Pradesh is 
primarily based on agriculture and horticulture. Over 
three-quarters of the workforce is engaged in these 
sectors. The state has a population density of 123 and a 
high literacy rate of 82.8%. Several rivers, including 
the Sutlej and Ravi, flow through Himachal Pradesh, 
offering vast hydroelectric potential. The region is also 
famous for its tourism, with places like Khajjiar 
(known as the "Switzerland of India"), Kullu, Kangra, 
Shimla, Dalhousie, and Dharamshala.

Indian Geography.q: Match List-I with List-II: List-I (Peaks) List-II (Mountain Ranges) A. Guru Shikhar 1. Nilgiri B. Doddabetta 2. Eastern Ghats C. Armakonda 3. Satpura D. Dhupgarh 4. Aravalli Choose the correct answer : A B C D

(A) Seasonal flow pattern of water (B) River systems vary due to climatic conditions (C) River systems are mathematically represented using Qmax (D) Narmada and Jhelum have similar river systems Choose the most appropriate answer:

A river system represents the seasonal flow

Indian Geography.q: Which waterfalls are associated with the Narmada River? (A) Mandhar (B) Hiran (C) Tawa (D) Dardi (E) Sahastradhara Choose the correct option:
Indian Geography.explanation:
Mandhar, Dardi, and Sahastradhara 
waterfalls are associated with the Narmada River. The 
Narmada flows through a fault valley, creating several 
significant waterfalls. The Kapil Dhara waterfall, 
located in Madhya Pradesh's Anuppur district, is a 
famous waterfall on the Narmada River. 
Some of India's notable waterfalls are: 
• Kunchikal Falls (455 m) – Shimoga, Karnataka 
• Nohkalikai Falls (340 m) – Meghalaya 
• Jog Falls/Mahatma Gandhi Falls – Sharavati 
River, Karnataka

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following statements about the 'Doabs' of Punjab are correct? (A) Jalandhar Doab is located between the Beas and Sutlej rivers. (B) Bari Doab is located between the Beas and Ravi rivers. (C) Sindh Doab is located between the Ravi and Jhelum rivers. (D) Chaj Doab is located between the Beas and Ravi rivers. Select the correct answer from the options below:
Indian Geography.explanation:
Jalandhar Doab is situated between the Beas 
and Sutlej, and Bari Doab is situated between the Beas 
and Ravi. These were formed by the depositional 
activities of the Sutlej, Beas, and Ravi rivers. This 
region extends approximately 640 km in length from 
northeast to southwest and 300 km in width from 
west to east, covering an area of about 1.75 lakh 
square km. Some other important Doabs are: 
 • Rechna Doab – Between the Ravi and Chenab 
rivers. 
• Chaj Doab – Between the Chenab and Jhelum 
rivers. 
• Sindh Sagar Doab – Between the Jhelum, 
Chenab, and Indus rivers.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following pairs is incorrectly matched? (A) Kosi – Subsequent River (B) Narmada – Rift Valley River (C) Sutlej – Antecedent River (D) Ghaggar – Endorheic River Select the correct answer from the options below:
Indian Geography.explanation:
Kosi River is not an example of a 
subsequent river; it is an antecedent river. The 
Narmada is a rift valley river, the Sutlej is an 
antecedent river, and the Ghaggar is an endorheic 
river. The Kosi River, a tributary of the Ganges, is 
known as the "Sorrow of Bihar" due to its frequent 
course changes, causing annual floods in Bihar.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rivers is not a tributary of the Yamuna River?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Tangri (or Dangri) River is a tributary 
of the Ghaggar (Haryana), whereas the tributaries of 
the Yamuna River include Tons, Giri, Asan, and Bata. 
The Yamuna River (1,384 km in length, drainage 
area 366,223 sq. km) originates from the Yamunotri 
Glacier and is the major tributary of the Ganges. In the 
plains, the Yamuna receives the Chambal, Sindh, 
Betwa, and Ken rivers from the south, and the Hindon, 
Rihand, Sengar, Nan, Baruna, and SasurKhaderi from 
the north.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following regions are highly prone to earthquakes? A. Tripura B. Northern Bihar C. Eastern Gujarat D. Haryana Select the correct answer from the options below:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The regions highly prone to earthquakes are 
Tripura and Northern Bihar. Based on seismic 
intensity, the West (Seismic Zoning Map) has divided 
India into three seismic zones:

Indian Geography.explanation: December 11, 1968 – Koyna

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following moutain passes is located in the Laddakh mountain range?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Khardung La is located in the Ladakh 
Mountain Range in the Union Territory of Ladakh, 
India. It is situated north of Leh and connects the 
Shyok Valley to the Nubra Valley. 
• Banihal Pass – Located in the Pir Panjal Range 
in Jammu & Kashmir. Due to heavy snowfall in 
winter, a tunnel named Jawahar Tunnel was 
constructed in 1956 to maintain connectivity. 
• Jelep La Pass – Located in the Greater 
Himalayas in Sikkim. It connects Chumbi Valley 
(Tibet, China) to India, facilitating trade between 
the two countries.

Indian Geography.explanation:
The correct sequence of the Kashmir 
Himalaya mountain range from north to south is 
Karakoram → Ladakh → Zanskar → Pir Panjal.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following states is not a part of the Ganga basin?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Sikkim is not a part of the Ganga basin. The 
Teesta River, a tributary of the Brahmaputra, flows in 
Sikkim. Hence, Sikkim belongs to the Brahmaputra 
basin, while Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, and Himachal 
Pradesh are part of the Ganga basin.

Indian Geography.q: The Western Ghats are also known as:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Western Ghats are also known as the 
Sahyadri Range. The Sahyadri is divided into Northern 
Sahyadri and Southern Sahyadri, separated by the 
16°N latitude, which passes through Goa.

Indian Geography.q: The Shevaroy Hills are located in:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Shevaroy Hills are located in Tamil 
Nadu. They are part of the Tamil Nadu Plateau, which 
lies between the Southern Sahyadri and the Tamil 
Nadu coastal plains.

Indian Geography.q: Which mountain range separates the Gangetic Plain and the Deccan Plateau?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Vindhya Range separates the Gangetic 
Plain from the Deccan Plateau. The major watershed 
divide in India runs through the Western Ghats, 
Satpura, Vindhya, and Aravalli ranges.

Indian Geography.q: The Chambal River Valley in Madhya Pradesh is an example of:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Chambal River Valley is known for its 
badland topography formed due to erosion. Chambal 
originates near Mhow in Madhya Pradesh and flows 
northwards, forming deep ravines before merging with 
the Yamuna River.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rivers does not form a delta?
Indian Geography.explanation:
According to commission, the correct 
answer is (d). 
The Narmada River does not form a delta. It 
originates from the Amarkantak Plateau and flows 
westward through a rift valley into the Arabian Sea, 
forming an estuary instead of a delta. 
Yamuna river is tributary of Ganga and it also doesn't 
form any type of delta.

Indian Geography.q: The highest peak in South India is:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The highest peak in South India is 
Anamudi (2,695 meters), located in the Anamalai 
Hills of the Western Ghats. The second-highest peak 
is Dodabetta (2,637 meters) in the Nilgiri Hills.

Indian Geography.q: In which part of the Himalayas do we find Karewa formations?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Karewa formations are found in the 
Kashmir Himalayas. These are lacustrine deposits 
that formed in the Pleistocene era. Karewa formations 
are important for saffron cultivation.

Indian Geography.q: The Garo-Rajmahal Rift was formed due to:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Garo-Rajmahal Rift was formed due 
to faulting. The Northeastern Plateau was originally 
part of the Peninsular Plateau but got separated due 
to tectonic movements during the formation of the 
Himalayas.

Indian Geography.q: Arrange the following places in the Kashmir Himalayas from north to south: 1. Srinagar 2. Gilgit 3. Kargil 4. Banihal
Indian Geography.explanation:
The correct order from north to south is: 
Gilgit → Kargil → Srinagar → Banihal

Indian Geography.q: The Main Boundary Fault (MBF) in Garhwal Himalayas passes through:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Main Boundary Fault (MBF) in 
Garhwal Himalayas passes through Rajpur in 
Dehradun district. 
Indian Geography 744• The Trans-Himalayas are separated from the

• The Great Himalayas are separated from the

• The Lesser Himalayas are separated from the

Indian Geography.q: The Main Boundary Thrust in the Himalayas Separates:
options: The Greater Himalayas from the Middle Himalayas
The Middle Himalayas from the Lesser Himalayas
The Lesser Himalayas from the Shivaliks
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Main Boundary Thrust (MBT) is 
located between the Lesser Himalayas and the Shivalik 
range. The Lesser Himalayas include ranges such as 
Dhauladhar, Pir Panjal, Nag Tibba, and Mahabharat. 
Notable tourist destinations like Shimla, Ranikhet, 
Chakrata, Mussoorie, Nainital, Almora, and Darjeeling 
are situated here.

Indian Geography.q: Arrange the Following Rivers in Descending Order of Their Length:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The correct order of rivers by length is: 
Godavari-Krishna-Yamuna-Kaveri 
• Godavari River: The longest river in South India 
(approx. 1,465 km), originating from the Trimbak 
Hills in Nashik, Maharashtra. It is also known as 
the "Dakshin Ganga" (Ganges of the South). 
Major tributaries: Pranhita, Purna, Pravara, 
Penganga, Manjra, Indravati, and Wardha. 
• Yamuna River: A tributary of the Ganges, 
originating from the Yamunotri Glacier (approx. 
1,384 km). It merges with the Ganges at 
Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. 
• Krishna River: The second-longest river in 
peninsular India (approx. 1,401 km). 
• Kaveri River: Known as the "Ganges of South 
India," its basin is called the "Rice Bowl of South 
India." It is around 800 km long.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the Following is the Newest Mountain Range in India?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Shivalik Range is the youngest 
mountain range in India, formed between the Middle 
Miocene and Pleistocene epochs. It is also called the 
Outer Himalayas or Sub-Himalayas, extending from 
the Potwar Basin in Punjab to the Kosi River in the east. 
Formation Order of Himalayan Ranges (From Oldest 
to Newest):

Indian Geography.q: Which Rock System is the Primary Source of India's Coal Deposits?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Gondwana Rock System is the main source 
of India's coal deposits. More than 90% of India's 
coal is found in these rocks, which were formed 
between the Upper Carboniferous and Jurassic periods. 
These sedimentary rocks contain fossils of fish and 
reptiles.

Indian Geography.q: Which is the Oldest Mountain Range in India?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Aravalli Range is the oldest mountain 
range in India, formed during the Pre-Cambrian era 
from quartzite, gneiss, and schist rocks. It is one of the 
oldest mountain systems in the world. The highest 
peak, Guru Shikhar (1,722 m), is located in Mount 
Abu, Rajasthan. Due to extensive erosion, only 
remnants of this ancient mountain range remain today.

Indian Geography.q: In Which River Valley are Gondwana Rocks Found?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Gondwana rocks are found in the 
Mahanadi River Valley. These rock formations are 
famous for their coal reserves and were formed by 
sediment deposition in river valleys. They are widely 
found in the Damodar Valley, Mahanadi Valley, 
Godavari Valley, Rajmahal Hills, Satpura, and 
Mahadeo Hills.

Indian Geography.q: The Highest Point in Peninsular India is:
Indian Geography.explanation:
Anamudi (2,696 m) is the highest peak in 
Peninsular India, located in the Anamalai Hills. It is 
formed by the confluence of: 
• Anamalai Hills (North) 
• Palani Hills (Northeast) 
• Cardamom Hills (South) 
• The second-highest peak in South India is 
Doddabetta (2,637 m), located in the Nilgiri Hills, 
where the Western and Eastern Ghats meet.

Indian Geography.explanation:
All of the above 
The Deccan Trap was formed during the Cretaceous 
period due to extensive volcanic eruptions in the 
Vidarbha region. It covers an area of approximately 
500,000 sq. km. It is mainly found in Maharashtra, 
Gujarat, and Madhya Pradesh, with some 
extensions into Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, and Tamil 
Nadu.

Indian Geography.explanation:
Zoji La Pass connects Srinagar to Leh. It

Indian Geography.q: What type of soil erosion occurs in the ravines (badlands) of the Chambal and Yamuna rivers?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Gully erosion occurs in the ravines of the 
Chambal and Yamuna rivers. These ravines, shaped 
like ‘U’ and ‘V’ or tunnel-like formations, are the most 
affected areas of gully erosion. Apart from these, such 
ravines are also found in Tamil Nadu and West 
Bengal. Every year, approximately 8,000 hectares of 
land turn into badlands.

Water-induced soil erosion is the most destructive and 
widespread. It primarily occurs in three forms:

Indian Geography.q: What type of rural settlements are found in the mountainous regions of India?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Dispersed settlements are found in the 
mountainous regions of India. 
Classification of human settlements: 
Based on their location, form, pattern, physical 
environment, economic, social, and cultural aspects, 
rural settlements can be classified into two types:

Indian Geography.q: In which direction do most of the rivers in peninsular India flow?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Most of the rivers in peninsular India flow 
eastward because their main water divide is formed by 
the Vindhya, Satpura, and Western Ghats. These rivers 
generally drain into the Bay of Bengal, while a few 
flow into the Arabian Sea and some merge into the 
Ganga and Yamuna river systems. 
Classification of peninsular rivers based on 
drainage direction:

Indian Geography.q: Mandakini River merges with Alaknanda River at:
Indian Geography.explanation:
Mandakini River merges with Alaknanda 
River at Rudraprayag. It is one of the five confluences 
of the Alaknanda River, located in the Garhwal region 
of Uttarakhand. The famous Hindu pilgrimage site, 
Kedarnath, is located just 86 km away. 
(List of confluences and rivers merging there):

Indian Geography.q: The confluence of Bhagirathi and Alaknanda rivers is known as:
Indian Geography.explanation: Devprayag

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following is NOT a cause of flooding?
options: Highly meandering and sinuous river courses
Indian Geography.explanation:
Vertical wind deflation is not a cause of 
flooding. 
Causes of floods in India: 
Monsoon rains occur in heavy downpours, leading to 
floods. Deforestation, faulty agricultural practices, 
improper land use, unplanned settlements in 
floodplains, developmental activities disrupting natural 
drainage, large-scale deforestation, and excessive 
irrigation raising groundwater levels all contribute to 
flooding. Although floods occur worldwide, they are 
particularly frequent and damaging in South, 
Southeast, and East Asia, especially in China, India, 
and Bangladesh.

Indian Geography.q: Which Himalayan mountain ranges are separated by the Main Boundary Thrust (MBT)?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Main Boundary Thrust (MBT) 
separates the Lesser Himalayas and the Shivalik 
Range. 
• Main Central Thrust (MCT): Separates Greater 
and Lesser Himalayas. 
• Main Boundary Thrust (MBT): Separates 
Lesser Himalayas and Shivalik. 
• Himalayan Frontal Fault (HFF): Separates the 
Shivalik and the Indo-Gangetic Plain.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following river groups is correctly arranged in ascending order based on their lengths?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Beas (470 km) → Ravi (725 km) → 
Yamuna (1,376 km) → Ganga (2,525 km)

Indian Geography.q: Jog Falls, located in the Western Ghats, is a waterfall on which river?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Jog Falls is on the Sharavati River in 
Karnataka. The water plunges from a height of 253 
meters, creating a spectacular view. It consists of four 
smaller waterfalls—Raja, Rocket, Rorer, and Rani. Jog 
Falls has been renamed "Mahatma Gandhi Waterfall."

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about India’s cold desert?
options: The Indus River flows through this region.
It is located in the rain-shadow area of the Himalayas.
It is bounded by the Zanskar mountains in the south.
It has a vast diversity of saline (salt) lakes.
Indian Geography.explanation:
Cold deserts, such as Ladakh and 
Antarctica, are different from hot deserts. While 
Ladakh is an example of a cold desert, it does not have 
a vast diversity of saline lakes. About 97% of Earth's 
water is saline, but cold deserts are not particularly 
known for their saline lake diversity.

Indian Geography.q: Which is the highest peak in the Kumaon Himalayas?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Nanda Devi (7,817 meters) is the highest 
peak in the Kumaon Himalayas, located in 
Uttarakhand. The Kumaon Himalayas stretch between 
the Sutlej and Kali rivers, covering about 320 km in 
length and 38,000 sq. km in area. Major peaks in this 
region include Badrinath, Kedarnath, Trishul, Mana, 
Gangotri, Nanda Devi, and Kamet.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following is a biodiversity hotspot in India?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Indo-Burma is a biodiversity hotspot in 
India.

Indian Geography.q: In Rajasthan, which lake is also known as ‘Dhebar Lake’?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Jaisamand Lake, also called Dhebar Lake, is 
located in Udaipur, Rajasthan. It was built by Maharaja 
Jai Singh and is the largest artificial freshwater lake in 
Rajasthan. It has seven islands and is home to a rich 
variety of aquatic life, earning it the name "Lake of 
Seven Islands."

Indian Geography.q: In which region of the Aravalli range are the Roja Bhakar and IsranaBhakar hills located?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Roja Bhakar and IsranaBhakar hills are 
located in the Jalore region of the Aravalli range. The 
Aravalli hills are the oldest mountain range in India. 
They originated during the Vindhyan period as folded 
mountains. These hills extend for about 800 km from 
Palanpur (Gujarat) to Delhi, in a southwest to northeast 
direction, east of the desert region of Rajasthan. The 
range narrows and decreases in height as it moves 
northeast. Near Delhi, it is known as the Delhi Ridge, 
where its height is approximately 800 meters.

Indian Geography.q: Bhima and Tungabhadra are tributaries of:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Krishna River is the second-largest river 
in Peninsular India. It originates near Mahabaleshwar 
in the Western Ghats and flows southeast for 
approximately 1,401 km. It has a drainage area 
distribution of 27% in Maharashtra, 44% in Karnataka, 
and 29% in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh. 
Tungabhadra and Bhima are its major tributaries, along 
with Koyna, Yerla, Varna, Panchganga, Dudhaganga, 
Ghataprabha, Malaprabha, and Musi. The Krishna 
River forms a delta before merging into the Bay of 
Bengal.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rivers does not originate in India?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Sutlej River originates in Tibet, near 
Rakshastal Lake, close to Mansarovar Lake. It is a pre
Himalayan river known as LangchenKhambab in 
Tibet. Before entering India, it flows parallel to the 
Indus River for about 400 km. It cuts through the 
Zaskar range at Shipki La Pass and enters India in 
Himachal Pradesh. The Spiti River is its major 
tributary. The river later joins the Indus at Mithankot. 
The Bhakra-Nangal Project, Harike, and Sarhind canal 
systems are associated with this river.

Indian Geography.q: Consider the following statements: A. ‘Char’ and ‘Bil’ are distinct landforms of the Ganga Delta region. B. ‘Reh’ and ‘Kallar’ are found in the Bangar region. C. The Khadar region contains deposits of old silt. Choose the correct answer from the codes below:
Indian Geography.explanation:
‘Char’ and ‘Bil’ are unique landforms of the 
Ganga Delta region. ‘Reh’ and ‘Kallar’ are found in 
the Bangar region. The Khadar region is a floodplain 
where fresh alluvial deposits occur annually. In delta 
areas, elevated landforms are called ‘Chars,’ and 
marshy lands are called ‘Bil.’

Indian Geography.q: Makalu, Annapurna, and Gosainthan peaks are located in:
Indian Geography.explanation:
Makalu, Annapurna, and Gosainthan peaks 
are situated in the Central Himalayas. The Greater 
Himalayas, also known as the Great or Inner 
Himalayas, have an average height of 6,100 meters and 
a length of approximately 2,400–2,500 km, with a 
width of 25 km. This range extends in an arc from 
Nanga Parbat in the west to Namcha Barwa in the east. 
It includes other peaks like Mount Everest, 
Kanchenjunga, Dhaulagiri, Trishul, Badrinath, and 
Kedarnath.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following statements about the Peninsular Plateau of India are correct? (i) It has a variety of metallic minerals. (ii) Its northern edge is a constructive plate boundary. (iii) Its northwestern part is covered by fertile black soil. (iv) Only two perennial rivers flow in this region. Codes:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Peninsular Plateau contains many 
metallic minerals, and its northwestern region is 
covered with fertile black soil. However, not just two, 
but multiple perennial rivers flow here. The plateau’s 
northern edge is a destructive plate boundary, not a 
constructive one.

Indian Geography.q: In which part of the Himalayas are ‘Doon’ and ‘Dwar’ found?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Shivalik Range is the outermost and 
newest range of the Himalayas, also known as the 
Outer Himalayas or Sub-Himalayas. It extends from 
the Potwar Basin in Punjab to the Kosi River in the 
east (87°E longitude). This range was formed during 
the Middle Miocene to Lower Pleistocene period in the 
Cenozoic era. The valleys between the Shivaliks and 
the Middle Himalayas are called ‘Doon’ in the west 
and central regions and ‘Dwar’ in the east. Dehradun 
and Haridwar are examples of such valleys.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following is incorrectly matched? Valley (Valleys) - Location
Indian Geography.explanation:
Johar Valley is located in Uttarakhand, also 
known as ‘Milam Valley’ or ‘Gori Ganga Valley.’ 
Therefore, statement (d) is incorrectly matched.

Peninsular gneiss is also called Bengal gneiss.
India’s oldest rocks belong to the Archean group.
The central part of the Himalayas is composed of Archean rocks.

Indian Geography.q: ‘Pat land’ is a topographical feature of?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Chotanagpur Plateau is a series of plateaus 
of different elevations. The central-western part, with 
the highest elevation, is known as the Pat region. 
• Chotanagpur Plateau is a part of the central 
highlands, extending from Purulia district of West 
Bengal to Jharkhand’s Palamu, Dhanbad, 
Singhbhum, Hazaribagh, Santhal Pargana, Ranchi, 
Lohardaga, and Gumla districts. 
• It is divided into several parts. The northern side 
of the Damodar River consists of plateaus and 
hillocks, whereas the southern side includes the 
Ranchi Plateau.

Indian Geography.q: ‘Pat region’ is located in?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Chotanagpur Plateau

Indian Geography.q: The Western Ghats are an example of which type of mountain range?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Western Ghats were formed due to a 
massive fault in the region. The western part of the 
landmass sank, creating the sea. Over time, rainfall and 
erosion shaped these mountains.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following is the correct example of an intermontane plateau?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Intermontane plateaus are surrounded by 
mountains on all sides and form due to tectonic 
activities along with the formation of fold 
mountains. 
• The Tibetan Plateau is the highest and largest 
intermontane plateau, bordered by the Kunlun 
Mountains in the north and the Himalayas in the 
south. 
• Other examples include the Altiplano (Bolivia and 
Peru), Iranian Plateau (Asia Minor), Columbia 
Plateau (USA), and Mexican Plateau.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rivers is not an antecedent river?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Antecedent rivers are those that existed 
before the upliftment of the landmass. 
• Examples: Indus, Kali, Sutlej, and Brahmaputra. 
• Yamuna is not an antecedent river.

Indian Geography.q: Which river forms an estuary?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Narmada River originates from the western 
part of Amarkantak and flows through a rift valley 
between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges, forming an 
estuary near Bharuch before merging into the Arabian 
Sea.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rivers does not form a delta?
Indian Geography.explanation: Narmada.

Indian Geography.q: How many river basins have a drainage area of more than 20,000 square kilometers each?
Indian Geography.explanation:
There are 14 river basins with a drainage 
area exceeding 20,000 square kilometers.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rivers is referred to as a ‘biological desert’ due to high pollution levels?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Damodar River is highly polluted due to 
industrial and jute mills, turning it into a sewage-like 
stream. Thus, it is called a ‘biological desert.’ 
• Yamuna River is often referred to as ‘green soup’ 
due to its pollution.
