Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rivers is not included in the Ganga Action Plan?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Damodar River originates in Jharkhand 
and flows through West Bengal before merging with 
the Hooghly River. It was once known as the ‘Sorrow 
of Bengal’ before its development as a multipurpose 
river valley project. Unlike the others, it is not 
included in the Ganga Action Plan.

Indian Geography.q: The only active volcano in India is located in:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The only active volcano in India is located 
on Barren Island in the Middle Andaman, while 
Narcondam is a dormant volcano. The capital of 
Andaman and Nicobar, Port Blair, is situated in South 
Andaman. Mount Thulier is in Great Nicobar, Mount 
Harriet and Mount Coyob are in South Andaman, and 
Saddle Peak is the highest point in North Andaman.

Indian Geography.q: Karewa Valley is located in:
Indian Geography.explanation:
Karewas are lacustrine deposits found in the 
Kashmir Valley. They contain thick glacial deposits, 
moraines, and other sediments. These deposits are 
found at an altitude of 1500-1800 meters along the Pir 
Panjal ranges in Jammu and Kashmir.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following drainage patterns is being represented?
Indian Geography.explanation:
A dendritic drainage pattern resembles the 
branching of tree limbs. It is commonly found in areas 
where the terrain is relatively flat and the underlying 
rock formations show little structural control. This type 
of drainage pattern is seen in the Northern Indian 
plains, including the middle Ganga plain and rivers 
like Krishna and Godavari.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following pairs is incorrectly matched?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The correct matching is as follows: 
• Latur – Earthquake 
• Nashri – Landslide 
• Kandla – Cyclone 
• Bhuj – Earthquake

Indian Geography.q: Arrange the following states in decreasing order of average annual rainfall:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The correct sequence in decreasing order of 
average annual rainfall is: Assam → Bihar → Uttar 
Pradesh → Haryana. India’s average annual rainfall is 
between 112-125 cm. The regions with the highest 
rainfall include the Western Ghats and Meghalaya 
hills, while the lowest rainfall occurs in Ladakh and 
western Rajasthan.

Indian Geography.q: Short and swift rivers originating from the Western Ghats and draining into the Arabian Sea are examples of which drainage pattern?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The small and fast-flowing rivers originating 
from the Western Ghats and draining into the Arabian 
Sea exhibit a parallel drainage pattern. These rivers 
flow parallel to each other, following the regional 
slope. Examples include the Sharavati, Mandovi, 
Zuari, Periyar, Pamba, Kali, and Gangaveli rivers.

Indian Geography.q: The longest tributary of a river in India is:
Indian Geography.explanation:
Among the given rivers, the longest tributary 
is the Chenab (1180 km). It originates from the 
Baralacha Pass in the Greater Himalayas as two 
streams, the Chandra and Bhaga, which merge in 
Himachal Pradesh. The other rivers' lengths are: 
Jhelum (724 km), Ravi (725 km), and Beas (470 km).

Indian Geography.q: The Brahmaputra River originates from:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Brahmaputra River originates from the 
Chemayungdung Glacier in Tibet and flows eastward 
through the Kailash Range and the Greater Himalayas. 
It is known as the Tsangpo River in Tibet.

Indian Geography.q: Identify the correct north-to-south sequence of passes in the Western Ghats:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The correct north-to-south sequence of 
passes in the Western Ghats is: Thalghat → Bhorghat 
→ Palghat. 
• Thalghat connects Mumbai to Nashik. 
• Bhorghat connects Mumbai to Pune. 
• Palghat connects Kochi to Coimbatore.

Indian Geography.q: The Mahanadi River originates from:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Mahanadi River originates near Sihawa 
in Raipur, Chhattisgarh, and flows eastward into 
Odisha, forming a delta near Cuttack before emptying 
into the Bay of Bengal.

Indian Geography.q: Arrange the following Himalayan ranges in descending order of altitude:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The correct descending order is: 
Karakoram → Ladakh → Zaskar → Pir Panjal. 
• Karakoram is the highest range, home to India’s 
highest peak, Godwin Austen (K2).

Indian Geography.q: In which part of India is the Dandakaranya region located?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Dandakaranya region is in southeastern 
India, covering parts of Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and 
Andhra Pradesh. It is divided into Dandakaranya 
highlands and the Dandakaranya valley.

Indian Geography.q: The river that divides the Malwa and Deccan Plateaus in India is:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Narmada River divides the Malwa and 
Deccan Plateaus. It originates from the Amarkantak 
Plateau in Madhya Pradesh and flows through a rift 
valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges before 
emptying into the Arabian Sea.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following mountain passes is not located in the Himalayas?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Palghat Pass is not a Himalayan pass. It is 
located in Kerala between the Nilgiri and Annamalai 
ranges and connects Kochi to Coimbatore.

Indian Geography.q: As we move from the plains to the Himalayas, what type of mountains do we encounter?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Himalayas are fold mountains formed 
due to the collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates. 
Other major fold mountains include the Arakan, 
Sulaiman, Hindu Kush, Zagros, and Karakoram ranges.

Indian Geography.q: Which region in India contains the oldest geological rocks?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Dharwar region in Karnataka has the 
oldest rocks in India. These are rich in mineral 
resources and date back to the Archean era.

Indian Geography.q: In which part of India is the Dandakaranya region located?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Dandakaranya region is in southeastern 
India, covering parts of Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and 
Andhra Pradesh. It is divided into Dandakaranya 
highlands and the Dandakaranya valley.

Indian Geography.q: Given below are two statements. One is labeled as Assertion (A) the other is labeled as Reason (R): Assertion (A) : The Indo-Gangetic plain is one of the densely populated regions of the world. Reason (R): The Indo-Gangetic plain has fertile land and an abundance of water. Select the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Indo-Gangetic plain is one of the 
densely populated region of the world because the 
Indo-Gangetic plain has fertile land and an abundance 
of water.

Indian Geography.q: Identify the river of India which has the following characteristics: (A) It originates from the Amarkantak Plateau. (B) It is a tributary of Ganga river. (C) During the summer months, it has little water.
Indian Geography.explanation:
The son river is a south bank tributary of the 
river Ganga which originates from the Amarkantak 
Plateau. 
• The Narmada river is west flowing river which 
originates from Amarkantak plateau. 
• The Ramganga river, a major tributary of Ganga 
river originates from the doodhatoli ranges of 
garhwal near gairsain. It joins the Ganga river near 
kannauj 
• The Kosi river is an antecedent river with its source 
to the north of mount Everest in Tibet, where its 
mainstream Arun rises.

Indian Geography.q: In which of the following states of India is the Bomdi-La pass located?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Bomdi-La pass located in Arunachal 
Pradesh Bomdi-La pass connects Arunachal Pradesh 
with Lhasa, the capital city of Tibet.

Indian Geography.q: In which of the following states are the Bababudan Hills located?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Bababudan Hills are located in the state 
of Karnataka, which is a major producer of iron ore. 
Other iron ore-producing regions in Karnataka include 
Kudremukh, Bellary-Hospet, and Chitradurga district.

Indian Geography.q: Which part of the Himalayas is the longest from east to west?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Nepal Himalayas extend from the Kali 
River to the Tista River, covering a length of 800 km. 
This region is taller than the Kumaon Himalayas and 
contains the highest peaks, including Kanchenjunga, 
Makalu, and Mount Everest.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following is the correct south-to north sequence of Himalayan ranges?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The correct south-to-north sequence of the 
Himalayan ranges is: Shivalik → Lesser Himalayas 
→ Greater Himalayas. 
• The Shivalik Himalayas, also known as the Outer 
Himalayas or Sub-Himalayas, are the youngest and 
outermost range. 
• They extend from the Potwar Basin in the west to 
the Kosi River in the east (87°E longitude). 
• Their average elevation ranges between 900 to 
1,200 meters. 
• In different regions, they are known as the Jammu 
Hills (Jammu), and as the Dafla, Miri, Abor, and 
Mishmi Hills (Arunachal Pradesh).

Indian Geography.q: According to S.P. Chatterjee’s classification of India’s natural divisions, Maharashtra Plateau falls under which sub-division?
Indian Geography.explanation:
According to S.P. Chatterjee’s classification, 
the Maharashtra Plateau and Satpura Range fall under 
the Northern Deccan Plateau subdivision of the 
Peninsular Plateau. The Eastern Plateau includes the 
Chotanagpur Plateau, Baghelkhand Plateau, Mahanadi 
Basin, and the Dandakaranya region. The Southern 
Deccan Plateau includes the Karnataka Plateau and the 
Telangana Plateau.

Indian Geography.q: Match the mountain ranges in List-I with their respective states in List-II and choose the correct answer from the given options: List-I (Mountain Range) List-II (State) A. Himalayas (i) Rajasthan B. Vindhyachal (ii) Maharashtra C. Aravalli (iii) Jammu & Kashmir D. Sahyadri (iv) Madhya Pradesh Code: A B C D
Indian Geography.explanation:
The correct matching is: 
• Himalayas → Jammu & Kashmir 
• Vindhyachal → Madhya Pradesh 
• Aravalli → Rajasthan 
• Sahyadri → Maharashtra 
Thus, option (c) is correct.

Indian Geography.q: Which two mountain ranges are almost parallel?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Vindhyachal and Satpura ranges are 
almost parallel to each other. 
• The Satpura mountain range starts from the Rajpipla 
Hills in the west, between the Narmada and Tapi 
rivers, and extends in the east and northeast direction 
in the form of the Mahadeo and Maikal Hills up to the 
Chotanagpur Plateau. 
• The eastern boundary of the Satpura range is formed 
by the Rajmahal Hills. 
• The Satpura range is composed mainly of basalt and 
granite rocks. 
• The highest peak of Satpura is Dhoopgarh (1,350 
m), located in the Mahadeo Hills. 
• Another significant peak is Amarkantak (1,066 m), 
near which the Narmada River originates.

Indian Geography.q: What is the average elevation of the snowline in the northeastern Himalayas?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The average snowline in the northeastern 
Himalayas is 4,400 meters above sea level. Other 
snowline elevations are as follows: 
• Average snowline: 4,300 – 6,000 meters 
• Greater Himalayas: 4,500 – 6,000 meters 
• Western Himalayas: 5,800 meters

Indian Geography.q: Identify the correct north-to-south sequence of Himalayan mountain ranges:
options: Greater Himalayas, Middle Himalayas, Outer Himalayas, Trans-Himalayas
Middle Himalayas, Greater Himalayas, Trans-Himalayas, Outer Himalayas
Outer Himalayas, Middle Himalayas, Greater Himalayas, Trans-Himalayas
Trans-Himalayas, Greater Himalayas, Middle Himalayas, Outer Himalayas
Indian Geography.explanation:
The correct north-to-south sequence of 
Himalayan mountain ranges is: 
Trans-Himalayas → Greater Himalayas → Middle 
Himalayas → Outer Himalayas 
• Trans-Himalayas (also called Para Himalayas) 
include the Karakoram, Ladakh, Zanskar, and 
Kailash mountain ranges. 
• The Greater Himalayas contain the highest 
peaks such as Mount Everest, K2, and 
Kanchenjunga. 
• The Middle Himalayas include mountain ranges 
like Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar, and Mahabharat. 
• The Outer Himalayas (Shivalik Range) are the 
youngest and outermost mountain range, also 
called the Sub-Himalayas. 
• Major glaciers in the Trans-Himalayas include 
Siachen, Hispar, Biafo, and Baltoro.

Indian Geography.q: What do the basalt layers of the Deccan indicate?
options: Massive volcanic eruptions in the distant past
Indian Geography.explanation:
The basalt layers of the Deccan indicate 
massive volcanic eruptions in the distant past. The 
formation of the Deccan Traps occurred due to 
volcanic activity in peninsular India during the late 
Mesozoic era. These rock formations were created as a 
result of lava eruptions through fissures. Their 
formation is considered to have taken place between 
the Cretaceous and Eocene periods. These rocks are 
quite hard, and the disintegration of these rocks has led 
to the formation of black soil.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following is a major river of the Awadh Plain?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The plain north of the Ganges is divided into 
two parts: the western part is known as the Rohilkhand 
Plain, while the eastern part is called the Awadh Plain. 
The major rivers of the Awadh Plain are the Ghaghara 
and the Gomti. The Ghaghara River is well known for 
its course changes and devastating floods. Rice is the 
major crop grown in this region. The Ganga Plain 
extends across Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, and 
West Bengal.

Indian Geography.q: Where is the Nathu La Pass located?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Nathu La Pass, known for its strategic 
importance during the India-China war, is located in 
the Dogekya Range in the state of Sikkim. This India
China trade route, which had been closed since 1962, 
was reopened in 2006. It connects Darjeeling and the 
Chumbi Valley to Tibet. The Chumbi River flows 
through this pass. 
• The Jelep La Pass is also located in Sikkim. 
• In Jammu & Kashmir, passes such as Chang La, 
Karakoram Pass, Burzil Pass, and Pir Panjal Pass 
are situated.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following plateaus is not a part of the South-Central Highlands?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Malwa Plateau, Bundelkhand Upland, 
Central India Plateau, Eastern Rajasthan Uplands, and 
the Aravalli Range are part of the Northern Central 
Highlands. The Southern Central Highlands include 
the Vindhyan Escarpment, the Vindhya Range, and the 
Narmada Valley.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rivers flows through a rift valley?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Narmada River flows through a rift 
valley. It originates from the peak of Amarkantak in 
the Maikal Hills. Flowing between the Satpura Range 
in the south and the Vindhyan Range in the north, it 
carves out a deep gorge in the marble rocks and forms 
the famous Dhuandhar Waterfall near Jabalpur. The 
Narmada River basin spans Madhya Pradesh, 
Maharashtra, and Gujarat. It is the largest river in 
peninsular India that drains into the Arabian Sea.

Indian Geography.q: What is the primary reason for the conversion of irrigated farmland into saline land in India?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The primary reason for the conversion of 
irrigated farmland into saline land in India is over
irrigation. According to the Economics and Statistical 
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare 
(E.A.S.A.F.W.) during 2021-22 the net irrigated area 
was 77.9 million hectare out of which 47.3% by tube 
wells, 24% was accounted by canal 2.8% by tanks, 
13.2% by other wells and 12% irrigated by other 
source of irrigation

Indian Geography.q: Analyze the following statements and choose the correct answer from the given codes:
options: The Rihand Dam is built on a tributary of the Son River.
The Hirakud Dam is built on the Mahanadi River.
The Tungabhadra project is a joint effort of Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka.
The Kosi River is known as the "Sorrow of Bihar."
Indian Geography.explanation:
All the given statements are correct, so an 
appropriate selection cannot be made.

Indian Geography.q: Through which states does the Narmada-Tapti basin pass?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Narmada-Tapti basin passes through 
Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh. Several dams have 
been built on the Narmada River in Madhya Pradesh, 
including the Maheshwar Dam, Indira Sagar Dam, and 
Omkareshwar Dam. The Tapi River has the Kakrapar 
Dam and the Ukai Project in Gujarat.

Indian Geography.q: Through which group of states does the Chambal River flow?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Chambal River flows through Uttar 
Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan. Due to 
extensive water erosion by this river, ravine land 
(badland topography) has developed along its course. 
Major dams on the Chambal River include the Gandhi 
Sagar Dam, Rana Pratap Sagar Dam, Jawahar Sagar 
Dam, and Kota Barrage.

Indian Geography.q: What is the estimated area of coral reefs in India?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The estimated area of coral reefs in India is 
2,383.87 sq km. The four major coral reef regions in 
India are Lakshadweep, the Gulf of Mannar, the Gulf 
of Kutch, and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands. Some 
of the world’s major coral reefs include the Great 
Barrier Reef, the Red Sea Coral Reef, the Florida Reef, 
the Andros Coral Reef, and Saya de Malha.

Indian Geography.q: What percentage of India's total land area is highly susceptible to seismic hazards?
Indian Geography.explanation:
In India, 59% of the total land area is highly 
susceptible to seismic hazards. The Central Receiving 
Station and the National Seismological Data Center 
(N.S.D.C.) have been established in New Delhi to 
collect, analyze, and archive earthquake data.

Indian Geography.q: Where is the source of the Tapi River?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Tapi River originates from the hilly 
region of Multai in Madhya Pradesh. After flowing 
through Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, and Maharashtra, it 
forms an estuary near Surat and drains into the Arabian 
Sea in the Gulf of Khambhat. In Gujarat, the Kakrapar 
Dam and Ukai Project are situated on this river.

Indian Geography.q: Although the general slope of the Peninsular Plateau is towards the east, some rivers still flow westward. Identify them:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Narmada and Tapi Rivers flow 
westward in the Peninsular Plateau. 
• The Narmada River originates near the Amarkantak 
peak in the Maikal mountain range. It is the largest 
river in Peninsular India that drains into the 
Arabian Sea. 
• It flows through the rift valley between the 
Vindhya Mountains in the north and the Satpura 
Mountains in the south, forming an estuary near 
Bharuch in Gujarat before emptying into the Gulf 
of Khambhat.

Indian Geography.q: The Peninsular rivers of India are an example of which type of drainage pattern?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Himalayan Rivers are antecedent river and 
by nature it is perennial river because water flows 
throughout the year in these rivers. 
• Peninsular rivers are consequent river and by nature 
it is non perennial or seasonal.

Indian Geography.q: Between which rivers is the Rechna Doab located?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The region between two rivers is called a 
Doab. Some important Doabs are: 
• Sindh Sagar Doab – Between Indus and Jhelum 
• Chaj Doab – Between Jhelum and Chenab 
• Rechna Doab – Between Ravi and Chenab 
• Bari Doab – Between Beas and Ravi 
• Bist Sagar Doab – Between Beas and Sutlej

Indian Geography.q: Match List-I (Doabs) with List-II (Rivers) and choose the correct answer: List-I (Doabs) List-II (Rivers) A. Bist Doab (i) Beas & Ravi B. Bari Doab (ii) Chenab & Jhelum C. Rechna Doab (iii) Beas & Sutlej D. Chaj Doab (iv) Ravi & ChenabCode: A B C D
Indian Geography.explanation:
The correct match is: 
• Bist Doab – Between Beas and Sutlej 
• Bari Doab – Between Beas and Ravi 
• Rechna Doab – Between Ravi and Chenab 
• Chaj Doab – Between Chenab and Jhelum

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following hotspots is not located in the Western Ghats?
Indian Geography.explanation:
A biodiversity hotspot is a region with high 
species diversity that is under threat. The Sundarbans 
are located in the delta region of West Bengal and 
Bangladesh, not in the Western Ghats.

Indian Geography.q: Where is the Nathu La Pass located?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Nathu La Pass is located in the Dongkya 
Range of Sikkim. It gained strategic importance 
during the India-China War and was closed in 1962. 
However, it was reopened in 2006 for trade. This pass 
provides a route from Darjeeling to Tibet via the 
Chumbi Valley.

Indian Geography.q: Where does the Luni River drain?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Luni River originates from the 
Aravalli Range and has a total length of 320 km. Its 
important tributaries are the Bandi, Sukri, and Jawai 
rivers. This river disappears into the Rann of Kutch, 
so none of the given options are correct.

Indian Geography.q: What is the height of the highest peak in the Satpura Range?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Satpura Mountain Range extends 
from the Rajpipla Hills in the west to the Maikal 
Hills in the east and further connects to the 
Chotanagpur Plateau. 
• The highest peak is Dhoopgarh (1350 m), 
located in the Mahadeo Hills. 
• Another important peak is Amarkantak (1036 m).

Indian Geography.q: The highly metamorphosed formations of ancient crystalline and archaean systems are not found in which of the following states?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Highly metamorphosed formations of 
ancient crystalline and archaean systems are not 
found in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, and Jammu & 
Kashmir.

Indian Geography.q: What is the highest peak of the Karakoram Mountains?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Karakoram Mountain Range, also 
known as the "Backbone of High Asia," forms the 
international boundary between India, Afghanistan, 
and China. 
• The highest peak is K2 or Godwin-Austen (8611 
m), the second-highest peak in the world after 
Mount Everest.

Indian Geography.q: The Ganges Delta is an example of which type of delta?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Ganges Delta, spread between Hugli 
and Meghna rivers, is the world's largest delta, 
covering about 100,000 square kilometers. It has an 
arcuate (arc-shaped) formation.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rock groups is the oldest?
Indian Geography.explanation: The sequence of rock formations in India is:

Indian Geography.q: Which is the highest peak in the Karakoram Range?
Indian Geography.explanation:
K2 or Godwin-Austen (8611 m) is the 
highest peak in the Karakoram Range and the second
highest peak in the world. 
Indian Geography 756

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following is located farthest to the east in India?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Among the mountain ranges mentioned in 
the question, the Maikal Range is located farthest to 
the east. 
• The Maikal Range is the eastern extension of the 
Satpura range. It extends across Shahdol and 
Mandla in Madhya Pradesh and Bilaspur district in 
Chhattisgarh. 
• The Maikal Range is the eastern extension of the 
Satpura range. It extends across Shahdol and 
Mandla in Madhya Pradesh and Bilaspur district in 
Chhattisgarh. 
• The highest peak of this range is Amarkantak, from 
where the Narmada, Son, and Wainganga rivers 
originate. 
• Kanha National Park is located within the Maikal 
Range.

Indian Geography.q: What is the largest natural geographical feature of India?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The largest natural geographical feature of 
India is the Peninsular Plateau. 
• It is part of the ancient Gondwana land and has a 
triangular shape. 
• It covers an area of 1.6 million square kilometers. 
• Its average elevation ranges from 600 to 900 
meters. 
• The Meghalaya Plateau forms the northeastern 
part of this region.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rivers is NOT a tributary of the Godavari River?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Godavari River (1,465 km) is the 
largest river in Peninsular India. It originates from the 
Trimbakeshwar Hills in the Kalasubai mountain range 
of Maharashtra and flows through Maharashtra, 
Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, 
Chhattisgarh, and Odisha before emptying into the Bay 
of Bengal. 
• Its left-bank tributaries include Dudhana, Pranhita, 
Indravati, and Sabari. 
• Its right-bank tributaries include Pravara, Manjara, 
Manaia, and Kinnerasani. 
• The Godavari River has the Dowleswaram Anicut 
Dam near Rajahmundry. The Gosikhurd Project is 
built on its tributary, Wainganga, in Maharashtra. 
• The Manjara River has the Nizam Sagar Dam. 
• The Mahi River originates in Madhya Pradesh and 
flows through Rajasthan.

Indian Geography.q: The lowest place in India, Kuttanad, is located in:
Indian Geography.explanation:
Kuttanad, the lowest place in India, is 
located in the Alappuzha district of Kerala. 
• The world's lowest point is the Mariana Trench, 
while the world's highest peak is Mount Everest.

Indian Geography.q: Which is the largest river in Peninsular India?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Godavari River is the largest river in 
Peninsular India (1,465 km). 
• It is also known as the "Dakshina Ganga" or 
"Vridha Ganga" (Old Ganga). 
• It originates from Trimbakeshwar in Nashik district, 
Maharashtra, and flows southeastward, draining into 
the Bay of Bengal. 
• Its basin covers Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, 
Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Telangana, and Andhra 
Pradesh. 
• Its major tributaries include Wardha, Wainganga, 
Maner, Sabari, Purna, Dudhana, Penganga, 
Indravati, Pranhita, Tal, and Manjara.

Indian Geography.q: In which of the following valleys of the Himalayas is the Shipki La Pass located?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Shipki La Pass is located in the Sutlej 
Valley. 
• Shipki La Pass is situated in the Zaskar Range of 
Himachal Pradesh. 
• It connects Shimla to Tibet. 
• The Sutlej River enters India through this pass.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following pairs is incorrectly matched? List-I (Doabs) List-II (Rivers)
Indian Geography.explanation:
Hills State 
Palkonda Hills Andhra Pradesh 
Jawadi Hills Tamil Nadu 
Kaimur Hills Madhya Pradesh 
Rajgir Hills Bihar

Indian Geography.q: According to the Indus Water Treaty (1960), India can use only ----- percent of the Indus River's water.
Indian Geography.explanation:
According to the Indus Water Treaty (1960), 
India can use only 20% of the Indus River's water. 
• This treaty was signed between India and 
Pakistan. 
Indian Geography 757

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following is a Caledonian mountain?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The mountains formed during the 
Caledonian orogeny belong to the Silurian and 
Devonian periods. 
• In India, the Aravalli, Satpura, and Mahadeo 
ranges are significant mountains of this period.

Indian Geography.q: In the Greater Himalayas, the snowline is higher in the west and lower in the east. The reason for this is:
Indian Geography.explanation:
In the Greater Himalayas, the snowline is 
higher in the west and lower in the east due to 
differences in humidity. 
• The altitude of the snowline in the Himalayas is 
as follows: 
° Average snowline: 4,300–6,000 meters 
° Great Himalayas: 4,500–6,000 meters 
° Western Himalayas: 5,800 meters 
° Eastern Himalayas: 4,300 meters

Indian Geography.q: The deepest river valley is found in:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The deepest river valley is found in 
Bhagirathi and Alaknanda. At the confluence of 
Bhagirathi and Alaknanda, Devprayag is located, 
where these rivers merge and flow together under the 
name Ganga.

Indian Geography.q: The Krishna River originates near which of the following locations?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Krishna River is the second-largest river 
in peninsular India and the third-largest in India. It 
originates near the Mahabaleshwar peak in 
Maharashtra and flows through Maharashtra, 
Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh, forming a 
delta before merging into the Bay of Bengal.

Indian Geography.q: The Eastern and Western Ghats meet at:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Eastern Ghats and the Western Ghats 
meet at the Nilgiri Hills. The highest peak in the 
Nilgiri Hills is Doddabetta (2,637 m), which is the 
second-highest peak in South India. The Nilgiri range 
extends across Tamil Nadu and Kerala.

Indian Geography.q: The Kali Sindh River is a tributary of which river?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Yamuna River originates from the 
Yamunotri Glacier and has a total length of 1,370 km. 
The right-bank tributaries of the Yamuna River include 
Chambal, Sindh, Betwa, and Ken Rivers. In ancient 
times, it flowed west of the Aravalli Hills into the Thar 
Desert, possibly as a tributary or main branch of the 
Saraswati River. The cities of Delhi, Mathura, and 
Agra are located on its banks. Kali sindh is tributary of 
river Chambal and Chambal is tributary of river 
Yamuna.

Indian Geography.q: What is the approximate length of the Himalayas from west to east?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The length of the Himalayas from west to 
east is approximately 2,500 km. 
• The Himalayas stretch across the northern and 
northeastern parts of the Indian subcontinent. 
• They are fold mountains primarily composed of 
sedimentary rocks, formed due to Alpine orogeny 
during the Tertiary period. 
• The Himalayas were formed by the collision of the 
Indian and Eurasian plates, compressing the 
sediments of the Tethys Sea between them.

Indian Geography.q: Which type of soil has the largest coverage in India?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Alluvial soil has the largest coverage in 
India. It covers approximately 43.4% (around 1.5 
million square kilometers) of the total land area. This 
soil is spread across the vast plains from Punjab to 
Assam, as well as in the valleys of the Narmada, Tapi, 
Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri rivers, along 
with coastal areas of Kerala. Other soil types include 
red soil (18.6%), black soil (15.2%), laterite soil 
(3.7%), and other soils (17.9%).

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following is an antecedent river?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Brahmaputra River cuts through the 
Greater Himalayas, forming the Tsangpo Gorge, 
before entering India, which is evidence of its 
antecedent nature. 
Brahmputra river originates from chemayangdung 
glacier of the Kailash range near the Mansarovar lake. 
The Brahmputra enters into Bangladesh near Dhubri 
and flows south ward. The Tista joins it on its right 
bank from where it is known as the Jamuna. It finally 
Indian Geography 758merges with the river Padma, which falls in the Bay of 
Bengal. 
Left Bank Tributaries - Burhi Dihing and Dhansari 
Right Bank Tributaries- Subansiri, Kamenh, Manas 
and Sankosh. 
In Tibet region it is known as Tsangpo, which means 
the purifier. Rango is the major right bank tributory of 
this river in Tibet.

Indian Geography.q: After joining the Teesta River, the Brahmaputra River is known as:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Brahmaputra River flows west of the 
Garo Hills and enters Bangladesh, where it is called 
the Jamuna River. The Teesta River, originating from 
Sikkim and joins the Jamuna River in Bangladesh. 
Further downstream, the Jamuna River merges with 
the Padma River. After this, the Meghna River, 
originating from the northeastern hills of Bangladesh, 
joins the Padma River, and together, they flow as the 
Meghna River, forming a delta before entering the 
Bay of Bengal.

Indian Geography.q: Name the pass located in the Lesser Himalayas:
Indian Geography.explanation:
Baramulla 
The Lesser or Middle Himalayas include passes like 
Pir Panjal, Banihal, and Baramulla. This range extends 
parallel between the Great Himalayas to the north and 
the Shivalik Himalayas to the south. To the southeast 
of this range lies the Dhauladhar range, on which 
Shimla is situated. Other important towns located in 
this range include Chakrata, Mussoorie, Nainital, 
Ranikhet, Almora, Darjeeling, and Dalhousie. Two 
major valleys exist between the Middle and Great 
Himalayas, with the Kashmir Valley lying between the 
Pir Panjal range and the Great Himalayas.

Indian Geography.q: The Garo, Khasi, and Jaintia hills are part of which of the following?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Deccan Plateau 
The Garo, Khasi, and Jaintia hills are part of the 
Deccan Plateau. They separated from the Deccan 
Plateau due to tectonic movements, creating the Malda 
Gap. The deposition of sediments in this gap led to the 
formation of the plains of West Bengal.

Indian Geography.q: Baba Budan Hills D. Meghalaya Code : 1 2 3 4
Indian Geography.explanation:
The correct matching is: 
Hills State 
Mikir Hills Assam 
Amarkantak Madhya Pradesh 
Khasi Hills Meghalaya 
Baba Budan Hills Karnataka 
Thus, option (c) is the correct answer.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following passes connects Arunachal Pradesh with Tibet?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Bomdila 
The Bomdila Pass is located in the northwestern part 
of Arunachal Pradesh. It serves as a route from the 
Tawang Valley to Tibet and connects Arunachal 
Pradesh with Lhasa, the capital of Tibet.

Indian Geography.q: In which of the following regions are Quaternary system rocks not found?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Karnataka 
Quaternary system rocks are not found in Karnataka. 
These rocks were formed during the Pleistocene and 
Holocene epochs, which are part of the Quaternary 
period. The deposits from these periods mainly consist 
of unconsolidated sediments and are found in various 
regions such as the Thar Desert, Rann of Kutch, 
Middle Ganga Plains, and Kashmir.

Indian Geography.q: In which geological period did the upliftment of the Himalayas first begin?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Middle Oligocene 
The first phase of the upliftment of the Himalayas 
began during the Middle Oligocene period. This 
upliftment started due to the collision of the Indian 
Plate with the Eurasian Plate. The Oligocene period 
spans from approximately 40 million to 25 million 
years ago and is part of the Tertiary Era. This era is 
known as the "orogenic period," during which 
mountain-building processes were actively occurring. 
• The Great Himalayas were formed during the 
Oligocene period 
• The lesser Himalayas were formed during the 
Miocene period. 
Indian Geography 759

Indian Geography.q: Which is the major river flowing in Jammu and Kashmir?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Indus river originates from a glacier near 
Bokhar Chu in the Tibetan region at an altitude of 
4,164m in the Kailash mountain range near Mansarovar 
lake. It discharges into the Arabian sea, east of Karachi.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following passes is located in Sikkim?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Nathu La Pass, which gained strategic 
importance during the India-China war, is located in the 
Dongkyala Range of Sikkim. It is situated at an altitude 
of approximately 1,431 meters above sea level. This 
pass was part of an ancient branch of the Silk Route. 
The India-China trade route, closed since 1962, was 
reopened in 2006. This pass provides a route to Tibet 
via Darjeeling and the Chumbi Valley, through which 
the Chumbi River flows. The Jalep La Pass is also 
located in Sikkim. In Ladakh, notable passes include 
Chang La, Karakoram Pass, Churji La, and Pir Panjal 
Pass is located in J & K.

Indian Geography.q: In which state is the Birmingham Canal located?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Birmingham Canal is a freshwater 
transport canal with a length of 796 km. It runs parallel 
to the Coromandel Coast, extending from the East 
Godavari district of Andhra Pradesh to Veluppuram in 
Tamil Nadu.

Indian Geography.q: In India, an example of badland topography is
Indian Geography.explanation:
A landscape where rivers cut numerous gullies 
and ravines into the plateau surface is known as badland 
topography. In the Chambal Basin, such land is referred 
to as ravine land.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following is not a tributary of the Indus River?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Indus River originates from a glacier near 
Bokhar-Chu in the Kailash mountain range in Tibet, at 
an altitude of 4,164 meters. In Tibet, it is called 
SingiKhamban or Lion's Mouth. The total length of the 
Indus River is 2,880 km, but in India, its actual length is 
only 709 km.

Indian Geography.q: Which river flows into the Arabian Sea?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Narmada River originates from the 
Amarkantak hills in Madhya Pradesh and flows into the 
Gulf of Khambhat near Bharuch in the Arabian Sea. Its 
total length is approximately 1,312 km, with a drainage 
area of 98,796 square km. The Vindhya Range lies to its 
north, and the Satpura Range is to its south. Along its 
course in Madhya Pradesh, the river passes through 
marble rocks, creating a beautiful scenic view.

Indian Geography.q: The tank irrigation system is common in -
Indian Geography.explanation:
In peninsular India, the primary irrigation 
method is tank or pond irrigation. The highest use of 
this system is found in Tamil Nadu. According to the 
Economics and Statistical Ministry of Agriculture and 
Farmers Welfare (E.A.S.A.F.W.) during 2021-22 the 
net irrigated area was 77.9 million hectare out of which 
47.3% by tube wells, 24% was accounted by canal 2.8% 
by tanks, 13.2% by other wells and 12% irrigated by 
other source of irrigation

Indian Geography.q: Which river is known as the "Sorrow of Bihar"?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Kosi River originates near the Gosainthan 
peak, north of Mount Everest. The main branch of the 
river, called Arun, originates from this point. After 
flowing through multiple channels, it merges with the 
Ganga 32 km west of Manihari. The river is notorious 
for changing its course and causing sudden floods, 
resulting in massive destruction of life and property in 
Bihar, earning it the name "Sorrow of Bihar."

Indian Geography.q: The Deccan Trap is composed of –
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Deccan Trap is a triangular-shaped region 
spread south of the Tapi River. It was formed during the 
Cretaceous period of the Mesozoic era. It is bounded by 
the Satpura and Vindhya ranges in the northwest, the 
Mahadeo and Maikal ranges in the north, the Eastern 
Ghats in the east, and the Western Ghats in the west. This 
plateau is primarily composed of lava. Its average 
elevation is 600 meters. In the south, it reaches a height of 
1,000 meters, while in the north, it is only 500 meters high.

Indian Geography.q: Which is the river that has both its origin and mouth within the Indian Republic?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Godavari River has both its origin and 
mouth within India. The Brahmaputra, Indus, and Sutlej 
Rivers originate near Lake Manasarovar, which is now 
part of China. In contrast, the Godavari River originates 
in the Nashik district of Maharashtra and flows into the 
Bay of Bengal. It is the largest river in peninsular India. 
Its major tributaries include the Wainganga, Manjari, 
and Penganga rivers.

Indian Geography.q: Panaji is situated on the banks of which river?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Mandovi River originates from the 
Sahyadri Hills and flows into the Arabian Sea. Panaji, 
the capital of Goa, is situated on the banks of this river. 
Indian Geography 760

Indian Geography.q: On which river is the Shivanasamudra Falls located?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Shivanasamudra Falls is formed on the 
Kaveri River. The Sharavathi River features the Jog 
Falls, Gersoppa Falls, and Mahatma Gandhi Falls. The 
Chambal River has the Chulia Falls. The Pykara Falls is 
located in the Nilgiri region. The hydroelectric power 
station on the Kaveri River was the first in Asia, 
established in 1902.

Indian Geography.q: Which river originates from the Brahmagiri Hills in Kodagu district?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Kaveri River originates from the 
Brahmagiri Hills in the Mysore Plateau, located in the 
Kodagu district of Karnataka. It flows southeastward 
through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu before emptying 
into the Bay of Bengal near Kaveripattinam. Its 
drainage basin covers parts of Kerala, Karnataka, and 
Tamil Nadu. Its major tributaries include Hemavati, 
Lokapavani, Shimsha, and Arkavathi to the north, while 
Lakshmantirtha, Kabini, Suvarnavati, Bhavani, and 
Amaravati flow from the south.

Indian Geography.q: In which state are the Cardamom Hills located?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Cardamom Hills are located in Kerala and 
Tamil Nadu. They extend south of the Annamalai Hills. 
These hills are known for the cultivation of tea, coffee, 
bamboo, and cardamom.

Indian Geography.q: Which Indian state does not fall under Seismic Zone V (the highest seismic risk zone)?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Madhya Pradesh does not fall under India's 
Seismic Zone V (the highest risk zone). 
• The point within the Earth where an earthquake 
originates is called the hypocenter. 
• The point directly above it on the surface where the 
seismic waves first reach is called the epicenter. 
• The instrument used to record seismic waves is 
called a seismograph.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following states is not associated with the Mandovi, Madei, and Mahadayi rivers?
Indian Geography.explanation:
Kerala is not associated with the Mandovi, 
Madei, and Mahadayi rivers. These rivers are connected 
to Goa, Karnataka, and Maharashtra as they originate in 
the Western Ghats and flow into the Arabian Sea.

Indian Geography.q: Which river system dissects the Malwa Plateau?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Chambal, Betwa, Bina, and Ken river 
systems dissect the Malwa Plateau. The Malwa Plateau 
is bordered in the west by the Vindhya Range and its 
extensions. It covers an area of approximately 81,767 
square kilometers.

Indian Geography.q: On which of the following rivers is the 'Dhuandhar' waterfall located?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Dhuandhar Waterfall is located on the 
Narmada River in Madhya Pradesh. The Narmada 
Valley originates from Amarkantak. White marble 
rocks are found here. It is noteworthy that the Sardar 
Sarovar Dam is also built on this river.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following is known as the 'Lungs of the World'?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The equatorial evergreen forest is called the 
'Lungs of the World.' These forests extend between 5° 
and 10° latitude north and south of the equator. Due to 
high temperatures and heavy rainfall, trees such as 
Rosewood, cinchona, ebony, and rubber are found here.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following river basins has the largest area?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The drainage basin areas of the following 
rivers (in descending order) are: 
• Godavari: 313,000 sq km 
• Krishna: 259,000 sq km 
• Mahanadi: 142,000 sq km 
• Narmada: 98,795 sq km

Indian Geography.q: The Brahmaputra River in the Himalayas is an example of:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Brahmaputra River in the Himalayas is an 
example of antecedent drainage because antecedent 
rivers are those that existed before the uplift of the 
landmass. In India, the Indus, Brahmaputra, and Sutlej 
are examples of antecedent rivers. The Brahmaputra 
River originates from the Chemayungdung Glacier in 
the Kailash range of the Himalayas in Tibet at an 
altitude of about 5,150 meters.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rivers forms an estuary?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The important rivers flowing into the Bay of 
Bengal are Mahanadi, Godavari, Kaveri, and Hooghly. 
The Hooghly River forms an estuary. The Kolkata port 
is situated on the Hooghly River. Due to tidal 
conditions, the water level rises, allowing steamers to 
reach Kolkata easily.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The Teesta River is a tributary of the Ganges
The Ukai Dam Project is located on the Tapi River
The Coromandel coastal plain is wider than the Malabar coastal plain
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Teesta River originates in the Himalayas 
of Sikkim and flows southward into Bangladesh, where 
it joins the Brahmaputra. The Ukai Multipurpose 
Project was constructed on the Tapi River in Gujarat. 
The valleys between the Lesser Himalayas and the 
Shivaliks are called 'Duns' (e.g., Dehradun, Kothridun, 
Patlidun). The valleys to the east are called 'Dwar' (e.g., 
Haridwar).

Indian Geography.q: The Ranchi Plateau is an example of:
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Ranchi Plateau is a significant example of 
a raised peneplain. Before the Cretaceous lava flow, the 
entire Ranchi Plateau was a vast, flat surface. Later, in 
the Tertiary period, the plateau was uplifted by about 
305 meters. As a result, the 915-meter-high surface of 
this region represents a raised peneplain.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following is not an antecedent river?
Indian Geography.explanation:
An antecedent river is a river that existed 
before the uplift of the landmass. In simple terms, these 
rivers were already flowing before the geological uplift 
and are not affected by structural changes in the land. 
Most major Himalayan rivers, such as the Indus, Sutlej, 
Brahmaputra, Ganges, Ghaghara, Kali, Gandak, Kosi, 
and Teesta, are antecedent rivers.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following river basins in India has the highest annual water yield?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The annual water yield of these river basins is 
as follows: 
• Ganga: 468,700 million cubic meters 
• Brahmaputra: 627,000 million cubic meters 
• Indus: 79,500 million cubic meters 
• Godavari: 118,800 million cubic meters

options: Laterite soil of the Deccan Plateau

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rivers flows between the Ladakh and Zanskar mountain ranges?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Indus River flows between the Ladakh 
and Zanskar mountain ranges. It originates from the 
Kailash Glacier at an altitude of 5,000 meters. The 
Jhelum River originates from the Sheshnag Lake in 
Kashmir and flows 212 km northwest to join Wular 
Lake. The Sutlej River originates from the Rakshastal 
near Mansarovar Lake in the southern slopes of Mount 
Kailash. The Chenab River originates in the Lahaul 
region of Himachal Pradesh at an altitude of 4,900 
meters, from the confluence of the Chandra and Bhaga 
rivers.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The correct tributary pairings for these rivers 
are: 
• Ganga: Yamuna, Ramganga, Kali, Sharda, 
Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi, Mahananda. 
• Chambal: Kali Sindh, Parvati, Banas 
• Godavari: Penganga, Manjira, Sabari, Indravati, 
Purna 
• Krishna: Koyna, Bhima, Tungabhadra 
• Mahanadi: Tel, Ong, Jonk, Mand, Ib.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rivers is not included in the Ganga Action Plan?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Kosi River is not included in the Ganga 
Action Plan, while the others are. 
The Ganga Action Plan launched by Government of 
India in 1985, aimed to improve water quality to 
acceptable standards by preventing the pollution load 
from reaching the river. 
Namami Ganga programme was launched in June 2014. 
Initially the programme launched for the period of 
March 2021 but later extended up to March, 2026.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following regions in India is most affected by soil erosion?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Chambal Valley is the most affected by 
soil erosion due to ravine formation caused by gully 
erosion. 
The Chambal river originates from Mhow in the Malwa 
plateau of MP and flows north wards through a gorge 
upwards of Kota in Rajasthan where the Gandhisagar 
dam has been constructed. From Kota, it transverses 
down to Bundi, Sawai Madhopur and Dholpur and 
finally joins the Yamuna near Itawah UP. The Chambal 
is famous for its badland topography called the 
Chambal ravines.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rivers in India forms an estuary?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Narmada originates on the western flank 
of the Amarkantak plateau at a high of about 1057m. 
After flowing a distance of about 1312km, it meets the 
Arabian sea south of Bharuch, forming a broad 27km 
long estuary. The Sardar Sarovar Project has been 
constructed on the river. 
 The two major rivers flowing westward in India, 
Narmada and Tapi, form estuaries. The tributaries of the 
Narmada River include Hiran, Banjar, Shakkar and 
Tawa.

Indian Geography.q: Which of the following rivers does not originate from the Maikal range?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Maikal range is the source of the 
Mahanadi River (flowing southeast), Son River 
(flowing north), and Narmada River (flowing west). 
Tapi does not originate from this range.

Indian Geography.q: Statement (A): Willow trees are drying up in the Lahaul Valley of Himachal Pradesh. Reason (R): Due to aging, these trees have lost resistance against aphid pests. Codes:
options: Both A and R are correct, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are correct, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is correct, but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect, but R is correct.
Indian Geography.explanation:
Aphids are small insects that suck the sap 
from plants. They belong to the Aphidoidea family. In 
Himachal Pradesh’s Lahaul-Spiti Valley, these pests are 
found in abundance. Due to aging, the willow trees have 
lost resistance against aphid attacks, leading to their 
drying up. Thus, both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) 
correctly explains (A).

Indian Geography.q: What was the former name of the Karakoram mountain range located in Jammu and Kashmir?
Indian Geography.explanation:
The Krishnagiri mountain in Jammu and 
Kashmir was renamed the Karakoram Range. K₂ or 
Godwin-Austen is the world’s second-highest peak, 
standing at 8,611 meters.

Indian Geography.q: In which Indian state is the highest percentage of groundwater utilization found?
Indian Geography.explanation:
In terms of percentage of irrigated land, 
Punjab has the highest irrigation coverage, with 
approximately 99.60% of its land under irrigation. The 
next states in order are Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, West 
Bengal, and Tamil Nadu. Note: Currently, Punjab has 
the highest percentage of groundwater utilization.
